The discovered information is via a collection process.
The event activity is not mapped. See the activity_name attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

activity_id.description: The normalized identifier of the activity that triggered the event. Each event class defines its own set of activity values. Use 0 (Unknown) when the activity cannot be determined. Use 99 (Other) when the activity does not match any defined value, in which case activity_name must be populated with the source-specific label.

activity_name.description: The event activity name, as defined by the activity_id. When activity_id is 99 (Other), this attribute must contain the source-specific activity label. For all other activity_id values, this must match the caption defined for that activity_id enum value.

actor.description: The user, process, or service that initiated the activity on the host. For system-level events this is typically a process; for IAM events it is typically a user or role.

api.description: Describes details about a typical API (Application Programming Interface) call.

assessments.description: A list of assessments associated with the device.

attacks.description: An array of MITRE ATT&CK® objects describing identified tactics, techniques & sub-techniques. The objects are compatible with MITRE ATLAS™ tactics, techniques & sub-techniques.

attestation_list.description: One or more cryptographic attestation objects over an event, each providing integrity, authenticity, and non-repudiation. Independent attesters over the same event — for example a producer at write time and a downstream processor at ingest — each contribute a separate attestation, distinct from co-signers on a single attestation, which share its signatures array. Carried on the record_integrity profile; the object itself is domain-agnostic.

authorizations.description: Provides details about an authorization, such as authorization outcome, and any associated policies related to the activity/event.

category_name.description: The event category name, as defined by category_uid value: Discovery.

category_uid.description: The category unique identifier of the event. Each event class belongs to exactly one category. Producers and mappers must set this to the category defined by the event class being used.

cis_benchmark_result.description: The CIS Benchmark Result object captures results generated from benchmark evaluations as defined by the Center for Internet Security.

class_name.description: The event class name, as defined by class_uid value: Device Config State.

class_uid.description: The unique identifier of a class. A class describes the attributes available in an event. Producers and mappers must set this to the uid defined in the event class definition. For example, Detection Finding is 2004.

cloud.description: Describes details about the Cloud environment where the event or finding was created.

confidence.description: The confidence, normalized to the caption of the confidence_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

anyOf.description: The normalized confidence is unknown.
The confidence is not mapped to the defined enum values. See the confidence attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

confidence_id.description: The normalized confidence refers to the accuracy of the security control or alert. An analytic with a low confidence means that the alerts may be noisy or may not be malicious in nature.

confidence_score.description: The confidence score as reported by the event source. If confidence_id is 99 'Other', it should be the same as confidence if both are populated.

count.description: The number of events aggregated into this single record. Only populate for aggregate events. When set, start_time and end_time should also be provided to define the aggregation window.

device.description: The device that is being discovered by an inventory process.

disposition.description: The disposition name, normalized to the caption of the disposition_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

anyOf.description: The disposition is unknown.
Granted access or allowed the action to the protected resource.
Denied access or blocked the action to the protected resource.
A suspicious file or other content was moved to a benign location.
A session was isolated on the network or within a browser.
A file or other content was deleted.
The request was detected as a threat and resulted in the connection being dropped.
A custom action was executed such as running of a command script. Use the message attribute of the base class for details.
A request or submission was approved. For example, when a form was properly filled out and submitted. This is distinct from 1 'Allowed'.
A quarantined file or other content was restored to its original location.
A suspicious or risky entity was deemed to no longer be suspicious (re-scored).
A corrupt file or configuration was corrected.
A corrupt file or configuration was partially corrected.
A corrupt file or configuration was not corrected.
An operation was delayed, for example if a restart was required to finish the operation.
Suspicious activity or a policy violation was detected without further action.
The outcome of an operation had no action taken.
The operation or action was logged without further action.
A file or other entity was marked with extended attributes.
The request or activity was detected as a threat and resulted in a notification but request was not blocked.
Counted the request or activity but did not determine whether to allow it or block it.
The request was detected as a threat and resulted in the connection being reset.
Required the end user to solve a CAPTCHA puzzle to prove that a human being is sending the request.
Ran a silent challenge that required the client session to verify that it's a browser, and not a bot.
The requestor's access has been revoked due to security policy enforcements. Note: use the Host profile if the User or Actor requestor is not present in the event class.
A request or submission was rejected. For example, when a form was improperly filled out and submitted. This is distinct from 2 'Blocked'.

An attempt to access a resource was denied due to an authorization check that failed. This is a more specific disposition than 2 'Blocked' and can be complemented with the authorizations attribute for more detail.
An error occurred during the processing of the activity or request. Use the message attribute of the base class for details.
The disposition is not mapped. See the disposition attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

disposition_id.description: Describes the outcome or action taken by a security control, such as access control checks, malware detections or various types of policy violations.

duration.description: The elapsed time of the aggregation window in milliseconds, from start_time to end_time. Only populate for aggregate events (count > 1). The value should equal end_time - start_time.

end_time.description: The time of the most recent event in an aggregate (count > 1). Do not populate for discrete, point-in-time events - use time alone. Subclasses such as findings may redefine this for their own time-range semantics.

end_time_dt.description: The time of the most recent event in an aggregate (count > 1). Do not populate for discrete, point-in-time events - use time alone. Subclasses such as findings may redefine this for their own time-range semantics.

enrichments.description:
The additional information from an external data source, which is associated with the event or a finding. For example add location information for the IP address in the DNS answers:

[{"name": "answers.ip", "value": "92.24.47.250", "type": "location", "data": {"city": "Socotra", "continent": "Asia", "coordinates": [-25.4153, 17.0743], "country": "YE", "desc": "Yemen"}}]

firewall_rule.description: The firewall rule that pertains to the control that triggered the event, if applicable.

is_alert.description: Indicates that the event is considered to be an alertable signal. Should be set to true if disposition_id = Alert among other dispositions, and/or risk_level_id or severity_id of the event is elevated. Not all control events will be alertable, for example if disposition_id = Exonerated or disposition_id = Allowed.

malware.description: A list of Malware objects, describing details about the identified malware.

malware_scan_info.description: Describes details about the scan job that identified malware on the target system.

message.description: A human-readable description of the event, as defined by the source. This should be a concise, meaningful summary suitable for display in a UI or alert notification - not a raw log line. For example: "User john_doe logged in from 10.0.0.1." rather than a raw syslog string.

metadata.description: The metadata object describes the event producer, schema version, and processing information. Producers and mappers must populate metadata.product to identify the data source, and metadata.version to indicate the OCSF schema version used. Consumers rely on this to interpret the event correctly.

observables.description: The observables array surfaces key indicators and entities from the event or finding in a single, consistent location for downstream correlation and detection. Each entry references an attribute path within the event (e.g., src_endpoint.ip) along with its type and value, enabling consumers to extract IOCs without parsing the full event structure.

osint.description: The OSINT (Open Source Intelligence) object contains details related to an indicator such as the indicator itself, related indicators, geolocation, registrar information, subdomains, analyst commentary, and other contextual information. This information can be used to further enrich a detection or finding by providing decisioning support to other analysts and engineers.

policy.description: The policy that pertains to the control that triggered the event, if applicable. For example the name of an anti-malware policy or an access control policy.

raw_data.description: The original event/finding data as received from the source, before normalization into OCSF. Populate this with the verbatim log line, JSON payload, or other native format for forensic and debugging purposes. This field is not intended for structured querying - use the normalized OCSF attributes instead.

raw_data_hash.description: A fingerprint (hash) of the raw_data content. Use this to verify the integrity of the original event data or to deduplicate events.

raw_data_size.description: The size of the original event data (as captured in raw_data) in bytes, before OCSF normalization. Useful for metering and capacity planning.

risk_details.description: Describes the risk associated with the finding.

risk_level.description: The risk level, normalized to the caption of the risk_level_id value.

anyOf.description: The risk level is not mapped. See the risk_level attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

risk_score.description: The risk score as reported by the event source.

severity.description: The event/finding severity label, normalized to the caption of the severity_id value. When severity_id is 99 (Other), this attribute must contain the source-specific severity label. For all other values, this should match the caption defined for that severity_id enum value (e.g., "High" for severity_id: 4).

anyOf.description: The event/finding severity is unknown.
Informational message. No action required.
The user decides if action is needed.
Action is required but the situation is not serious at this time.
Action is required immediately.
Action is required immediately and the scope is broad.
An error occurred but it is too late to take remedial action.
The event/finding severity is not mapped. See the severity attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

severity_id.description:
The normalized identifier of the event/finding severity.

The normalized severity is a measurement the effort and expense required to manage and resolve an event or incident. Smaller numerical values represent lower impact events, and larger numerical values represent higher impact events.

start_time.description: The time of the earliest event in an aggregate (count > 1). Do not populate for discrete, point-in-time events - use time alone. Subclasses such as findings may redefine this for their own time-range semantics.

start_time_dt.description: The time of the earliest event in an aggregate (count > 1). Do not populate for discrete, point-in-time events - use time alone. Subclasses such as findings may redefine this for their own time-range semantics.

status.description: The event status label, normalized to the caption of the status_id value. When status_id is 99 (Other), this attribute must contain the source-specific status label. For all other values, this must match the caption defined for that status_id enum value (e.g., "Success" for status_id: 1).

status_code.description: The source-specific status or error code as reported by the event source. For example, a Windows logon failure code (0x18), an HTTP response code (403), or an AWS API error code. This preserves the original code for detailed troubleshooting beyond what status_id conveys.

status_detail.description: A human-readable description providing additional context about the event outcome. Use this to convey details that go beyond the normalized status_id and source-specific status_code, such as a failure reason or error message. For example: "Account locked after 5 failed attempts.".

anyOf.description: The status is unknown.
The activity completed successfully.
The activity failed.
The status is not mapped. See the status attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

status_id.description: The normalized status of the event outcome. Use this family of attributes to convey the outcome of the activity described by the event. Producers should map their source outcome to 1 (Success) or 2 (Failure). Use 0 (Unknown) when the outcome cannot be determined, and 99 (Other) with a populated status string when the source value does not map cleanly.

time.description: The primary timestamp of the event - when the activity actually occurred at the source. This does not capture when the event record was created or serialized by the source system; for event lifecycle timestamps such as ingestion and processing, use metadata.logged_time and metadata.processed_time respectively, or the equivalent attributes in the metadata.loggers array when recording pipeline stages. For aggregate events (count > 1), set this to start_time (the earliest OCSF time in the aggregate) to preserve causal ordering and consistent timeline alignment. Note: finding classes redefine time as the finding creation time rather than the activity occurrence time. This must be a UTC epoch value in milliseconds (e.g., 1776881335332). Mappers should use the most precise and authoritative timestamp available from the source.

time_dt.description: The primary timestamp of the event - when the activity actually occurred at the source. This does not capture when the event record was created or serialized by the source system; for event lifecycle timestamps such as ingestion and processing, use metadata.logged_time and metadata.processed_time respectively, or the equivalent attributes in the metadata.loggers array when recording pipeline stages. For aggregate events (count > 1), set this to start_time (the earliest OCSF time in the aggregate) to preserve causal ordering and consistent timeline alignment. Note: finding classes redefine time as the finding creation time rather than the activity occurrence time. This must be a UTC epoch value in milliseconds (e.g., 1776881335332). Mappers should use the most precise and authoritative timestamp available from the source.

timezone_offset.description: The number of minutes that the reported event time is ahead or behind UTC, in the range -1,080 to +1,080. This allows consumers to reconstruct the local time at the event source. For example, US Eastern Standard Time is -300. Populate this when the source provides local time zone information.

type_name.description: The event/finding type name, combining the class and activity (e.g., "Detection Finding: Create"). The value must match the class_name and activity_name joined by ": ".

anyOf.description: The discovered information is via a log.
The discovered information is via a collection process.

type_uid.description: The event/finding type ID. It identifies the event's semantics and structure. Producers and mappers must compute this as class_uid * 100 + activity_id. It uniquely identifies the combination of event class and activity across the entire schema. For example, Detection Finding: Create is 200401.

unmapped.description:
A container for source-specific attributes that do not map to any defined OCSF attribute. Use this to preserve valuable source data that would otherwise be lost during normalization. The keys and values are specific to the event source.

Note: Consumers should not rely on a stable structure within this field. The preferred approach to unmapped attributes is to create a custom extension with the desired structure.

OcsfConfigState.title: OcsfConfigState

OcsfContainer.description: The Container object describes an instance of a specific container. A container is a prepackaged, portable system image that runs isolated on an existing system using a container runtime like containerd.

hash.description: Commit hash of image created for docker or the SHA256 hash of the container. For example: 13550340a8681c84c861aac2e5b440161c2b33a3e4f302ac680ca5b686de48de.

image.description: The container image used as a template to run the container.

labels.description: The list of labels associated to the container.

name.description: The container name.

network_driver.description: The network driver used by the container. For example, bridge, overlay, host, none, etc.

orchestrator.description: The orchestrator managing the container, such as ECS, EKS, K8s, or OpenShift.

pod_uuid.description: The unique identifier of the pod (or equivalent) that the container is executing on.

runtime.description: The backend running the container, such as containerd or cri-o.

size.description: The size of the container image.

tag.description: The tag used by the container. It can indicate version, format, OS.

tags.description: The list of tags; {key:value} pairs associated to the container.

uid.description: The full container unique identifier for this instantiation of the container. For example: ac2ea168264a08f9aaca0dfc82ff3551418dfd22d02b713142a6843caa2f61bf.

OcsfContainer.title: OcsfContainer

OcsfContainerProfile.description: The container context for a process.

container.description: The information describing an instance of a container. A container is a prepackaged, portable system image that runs isolated on an existing system using a container runtime like containerd.

namespace_pid.description: If running under a process namespace (such as in a container), the process identifier within that process namespace.

OcsfContainerProfile.title: OcsfContainerProfile

OcsfCpuInfo.description: The CPU information object contains attributes describing a physical CPU package installed in the device.

cores.description: The number of processing cores or compute units for the component.

cpu_architecture.description: The CPU architecture, normalized to the caption of the cpu_architecture_id value. In the case of Other, it is defined by the source.

anyOf.description: The CPU architecture is unknown.
CPU uses the x86 ISA. For bitness, refer to cpu_bits.
CPU uses the ARM ISA. For bitness, refer to cpu_bits.
CPU uses the RISC-V ISA. For bitness, refer to cpu_bits.
The CPU architecture is not mapped. See the cpu_architecture attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

cpu_architecture_id.description: The normalized identifier of the CPU architecture.

cpu_bits.description: The number of bits used by the CPU for memory addressing.

model.description: The model name of the CPU. For example: Intel Xeon Gold 6348, AMD EPYC 7763, or Apple M3 Max.

speed_mhz.description: The nominal clock speed of the unit, expressed in megahertz.

vendor_name.description: The name of the vendor of the CPU. For example: Intel, AMD, or Apple.

OcsfCpuInfo.title: OcsfCpuInfo

OcsfCve.description: The Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVE) object represents publicly disclosed cybersecurity vulnerabilities defined in CVE Program catalog (CVE). There is one CVE Record for each vulnerability in the catalog.

created_time.description: The Record Creation Date identifies when the CVE ID was issued to a CVE Numbering Authority (CNA) or the CVE Record was published on the CVE List. Note that the Record Creation Date does not necessarily indicate when this vulnerability was discovered, shared with the affected vendor, publicly disclosed, or updated in CVE.

created_time_dt.description: The Record Creation Date identifies when the CVE ID was issued to a CVE Numbering Authority (CNA) or the CVE Record was published on the CVE List. Note that the Record Creation Date does not necessarily indicate when this vulnerability was discovered, shared with the affected vendor, publicly disclosed, or updated in CVE.

cvss.description: The CVSS object details Common Vulnerability Scoring System scores from the advisory that are related to the vulnerability.

cwe.description: The CWE object represents a weakness in a software system that can be exploited by a threat actor to perform an attack. The CWE object is based on the Common Weakness Enumeration (CWE) catalog.

cwe_uid.description: The Common Weakness Enumeration (CWE) unique identifier. For example: CWE-787.

cwe_url.description: Common Weakness Enumeration (CWE) definition URL. For example: https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/787.html.

desc.description: A brief description of the CVE Record.

epss.description: The Exploit Prediction Scoring System (EPSS) object describes the estimated probability a vulnerability will be exploited. EPSS is a community-driven effort to combine descriptive information about vulnerabilities (CVEs) with evidence of actual exploitation in-the-wild.

modified_time.description: The Record Modified Date identifies when the CVE record was last updated.

modified_time_dt.description: The Record Modified Date identifies when the CVE record was last updated.

product.description: The product where the vulnerability was discovered.

references.description: A list of reference URLs with additional information about the CVE Record.

related_cwes.description: Describes the Common Weakness Enumeration details related to the CVE Record.

title.description: A title or a brief phrase summarizing the CVE record.

type.description:
The vulnerability type as classified in the CVE catalog.

Most frequently used vulnerability types are: DoS, Code Execution, Overflow, Memory Corruption, Sql Injection, XSS, Directory Traversal, Http Response Splitting, Bypass something, Gain Information, Gain Privileges, CSRF, File Inclusion. For more information see Vulnerabilities By Type distributions.

uid.description: The Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures unique number assigned to a specific computer vulnerability. A CVE Identifier begins with 4 digits representing the year followed by a sequence of digits that acts as a unique identifier. For example: CVE-2021-12345.

OcsfCve.title: OcsfCve

OcsfCvss.description: The Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) object provides a way to capture the principal characteristics of a vulnerability and produce a numerical score reflecting its severity.

base_score.description: The CVSS base score. For example: 9.1.

depth.description: The CVSS depth represents a depth of the equation used to calculate CVSS score.

metrics.description: The Common Vulnerability Scoring System metrics. This attribute contains information on the CVE's impact. If the CVE has been analyzed, this attribute will contain any CVSSv2 or CVSSv3 information associated with the vulnerability. For example: { {"Access Vector", "Network"}, {"Access Complexity", "Low"}, ...}.

overall_score.description: The CVSS overall score, impacted by base, temporal, and environmental metrics. For example: 9.1.

severity.description:
The Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) Qualitative Severity Rating. A textual representation of the numeric score.

CVSS v2.0
  • Low (0.0 – 3.9)
  • Medium (4.0 – 6.9)
  • High (7.0 – 10.0)

CVSS v3.0
  • None (0.0)
  • Low (0.1 - 3.9)
  • Medium (4.0 - 6.9)
  • High (7.0 - 8.9)
  • Critical (9.0 - 10.0)

src_url.description: The source URL for the CVSS score. For example: https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2021-44228

vector_string.description: The CVSS vector string is a text representation of a set of CVSS metrics. It is commonly used to record or transfer CVSS metric information in a concise form. For example: 3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:H.

vendor_name.description: The vendor that provided the CVSS score. For example: NVD, REDHAT etc.

version.description: The CVSS version. For example: 3.1.

OcsfCvss.title: OcsfCvss

OcsfCwe.description: The CWE object represents a weakness in a software system that can be exploited by a threat actor to perform an attack. The CWE object is based on the Common Weakness Enumeration (CWE) catalog.

caption.description: The caption assigned to the Common Weakness Enumeration unique identifier.

src_url.description: URL pointing to the CWE Specification. For more information see CWE.

uid.description: The Common Weakness Enumeration unique number assigned to a specific weakness. A CWE Identifier begins "CWE" followed by a sequence of digits that acts as a unique identifier. For example: CWE-123.

OcsfCwe.title: OcsfCwe

OcsfD3fTactic.description: The Defensive Tactic object describes the tactic ID and/or name that is associated to an attack.

name.description: The tactic name that is associated with the defensive technique. For example: Isolate.

src_url.description: The versioned permalink of the defensive tactic. For example: https://d3fend.mitre.org/tactic/d3f:Isolate/

uid.description: The unique identifier of the defensive tactic.

uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

OcsfD3fTactic.title: OcsfD3fTactic

OcsfD3fTechnique.description: The Defensive Technique object describes the leaf defensive technique ID and/or name associated to a countermeasure.

name.description: The name of the defensive technique. For example: IO Port Restriction.

src_url.description: The versioned permalink of the defensive technique. For example: https://d3fend.mitre.org/technique/d3f:IOPortRestriction/

uid.description: The unique identifier of the defensive technique. For example: D3-IOPR.

uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

OcsfD3fTechnique.title: OcsfD3fTechnique

OcsfD3fend.description: The Defensive Countermeasure object describes the tactic & technique associated with a countermeasure.

d3f_tactic.description: The Tactic object describes the tactic ID and/or name that is associated with a countermeasure.

d3f_technique.description: The Technique object describes the technique ID and/or name associated with a countermeasure.

version.description: The D3FEND™ Matrix version.

OcsfD3fend.title: OcsfD3fend

OcsfDataClassification.description: The Data Classification object includes information about data classification levels and data category types.

category.description: The name of the data classification category that data matched into, e.g. Financial, Personal, Governmental, etc.

anyOf.description: The type is not mapped. See the data_type attribute, which contains a data source specific value.
Any Personally Identifiable Information (PII), Electronic Personal Health Information (ePHI), or similarly personal information. E.g., full name, home address, date of birth, etc.
Any sensitive government identification number related to a person or other classified material. E.g., Passport numbers, driver license numbers, business identification, taxation identifiers, etc.
Any financially-related sensitive information or Cardholder Data (CHD). E.g., banking account numbers, credit card numbers, International Banking Account Numbers (IBAN), SWIFT codes, etc.
Any business-specific sensitive data such as intellectual property, trademarks, copyrights, human resource data, Board of Directors meeting minutes, and similar.
Any mission-specific sensitive data for military, law enforcement, or other government agencies such as specifically classified data, weapon systems information, or other planning data.

Any sensitive security-related data such as passwords, passkeys, IP addresses, API keys, credentials and similar secrets. E.g., AWS Access Secret Key, SaaS API Keys, user passwords, database credentials, etc.
Any other type of data classification or a multi-variate classification made up of several other classification categories.

category_id.description: The normalized identifier of the data classification category.

classifier_details.description: Describes details about the classifier used for data classification.

confidentiality.description: The file content confidentiality, normalized to the confidentiality_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

anyOf.description: The confidentiality is unknown.
The confidentiality is not mapped. See the confidentiality attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

confidentiality_id.description: The normalized identifier of the file content confidentiality indicator.

discovery_details.description: Details about the data discovered by classification job.

policy.description: Details about the data policy that governs data handling and security measures related to classification.

src_url.description: The source URL pointing towards the full classification job details.

status.description: The resultant status of the classification job normalized to the caption of the status_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

status_details.description: The contextual description of the status, status_id value.

anyOf.description: The status is unknown.
The classification job completed for the evaluated resource.
The classification job partially completed for the evaluated resource.
The classification job failed for the evaluated resource.
The classification job type id is not mapped.

status_id.description: The normalized status identifier of the classification job.

total.description: The total count of discovered entities, by the classification job.

uid.description: The unique identifier of the classification job.

OcsfDataClassification.title: OcsfDataClassification

OcsfDataClassificationProfile.description: The Data Classification profile adds attributes to specific resource objects, allowing users to describe information about classifiers & data classification results.

data_classification.description: The Data Classification object includes information about data classification levels and data category types.

data_classifications.description: A list of Data Classification objects, that include information about data classification levels and data category types, identified by a classifier.

OcsfDataClassificationProfile.title: OcsfDataClassificationProfile

OcsfDataSecurity.description: The Data Security object describes the characteristics, techniques and content of a Data Loss Prevention (DLP), Data Loss Detection (DLD), Data Classification, or similar tools' finding, alert, or detection mechanism(s).

category.description: The name of the data classification category that data matched into, e.g. Financial, Personal, Governmental, etc.

anyOf.description: The type is not mapped. See the data_type attribute, which contains a data source specific value.
Any Personally Identifiable Information (PII), Electronic Personal Health Information (ePHI), or similarly personal information. E.g., full name, home address, date of birth, etc.
Any sensitive government identification number related to a person or other classified material. E.g., Passport numbers, driver license numbers, business identification, taxation identifiers, etc.
Any financially-related sensitive information or Cardholder Data (CHD). E.g., banking account numbers, credit card numbers, International Banking Account Numbers (IBAN), SWIFT codes, etc.
Any business-specific sensitive data such as intellectual property, trademarks, copyrights, human resource data, Board of Directors meeting minutes, and similar.
Any mission-specific sensitive data for military, law enforcement, or other government agencies such as specifically classified data, weapon systems information, or other planning data.

Any sensitive security-related data such as passwords, passkeys, IP addresses, API keys, credentials and similar secrets. E.g., AWS Access Secret Key, SaaS API Keys, user passwords, database credentials, etc.
Any other type of data classification or a multi-variate classification made up of several other classification categories.

category_id.description: The normalized identifier of the data classification category.

classifier_details.description: Describes details about the classifier used for data classification.

confidentiality.description: The file content confidentiality, normalized to the confidentiality_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

anyOf.description: The confidentiality is unknown.
The confidentiality is not mapped. See the confidentiality attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

confidentiality_id.description: The normalized identifier of the file content confidentiality indicator.

data_lifecycle_state.description: The name of the stage or state that the data was in. E.g., Data-at-Rest, Data-in-Transit, etc.

anyOf.description: The data lifecycle state is unknown.

The data was stored on physical or logical media and was not actively moving through the network nor was being processed. E.g., data stored in a database, PDF files in a file share, or EHR records in object storage.

The data was actively moving through the network or from one physical or logical location to another. E.g., emails being send, data replication or Change Data Capture (CDC) streams, or sensitive data processed on an API.

The data was being processed, accessed, or read by a system, making it active in memory or CPU. E.g., sensitive data in a Business Intelligence tool, ePHI being processed in an EHR application or a user viewing data stored in a spreadsheet or PDF.
The data lifecycle state is not mapped. See the data_lifecycle_state attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

data_lifecycle_state_id.description: The stage or state that the data was in when it was assessed or scanned by a data security tool.

detection_pattern.description: Specific pattern, algorithm, fingerprint, or model used for detection.

detection_system.description: The data security tool or system that the finding, detection, or alert originated from, normalized to the caption of detection_system_id. E.g., Endpoint, Secure Email Gateway, etc.

anyOf.description: The detection system type is Unknown.

A dedicated agent or sensor installed on a device, either a dedicated data security tool or an Endpoint Detection & Response (EDR) tool that can detect sensitive data and/or enforce data security policies. E.g., Forcepoint DLP, Symantec DLP, Microsoft Defender for Endpoint (MDE).

A Data Loss Prevention (DLP) gateway that is positioned in-line of an information store such as a network share, a database, or otherwise that can detect sensitive data and/or enforce data security policies.

A Mobile Device Management (MDM) or Enterprise Mobility Management (EMM) tool that can detect sensitive data and/or enforce data security policies on mobile devices (e.g., cellphones, tablets, End User Devices [EUDs]).
A tool that actively identifies and classifies sensitive data in digital media and information stores in accordance with a policy or automated functionality. E.g, Amazon Macie, Microsoft Purview.
A Secure Web Gateway (SWG) is any tool that can detect sensitive data and/or enforce data security policies at a network-edge such as within a proxy or firewall service.
A Secure Email Gateway (SEG) is any tool that can detect sensitive data and/or enforce data security policies within email systems. E.g., Microsoft Defender for Office, Google Workspaces.

A Digital Rights Management (DRM) or a dedicated Information Rights Management (IRM) are tools which can detect sensitive data and/or enforce data security policies on digital media via policy or user access rights.

A Cloud Access Security Broker (CASB) that can detect sensitive data and/or enforce data security policies in-line to cloud systems such as the public cloud or Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) tool. E.g., Forcepoint CASB, SkyHigh Security.
A Database Activity Monitoring (DAM) tool that can detect sensitive data and/or enforce data security policies as part of a dedicated database or warehouse monitoring solution.

A built in Data Loss Prevention (DLP) or other data security capability within a tool or platform such as an Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) or Customer Relations Management (CRM) tool that can detect sensitive data and/or enforce data security policies.

Any Developer Security tool such as an Infrastructure-as-Code (IAC) security scanner, Secrets Detection, or Secure Software Development Lifecycle (SSDLC) tool that can detect sensitive data and/or enforce data security policies. E.g., TruffleHog, GitGuardian, Git-Secrets.

A Data Security Posture Management (DSPM) tool is a continuous monitoring and data discovery solution that can detect sensitive data and/or enforce data security policies for local and cloud environments. E.g., Cyera, Sentra, IBM Polar Security.
The detection system type is not mapped. See the detection_system attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

detection_system_id.description: The normalized identifier of the data security tool or system type from which the finding, detection, or alert originated. When the type is not listed, use 99 (Other) and populate detection_system with the source-specific label.

discovery_details.description: Details about the data discovered by classification job.

pattern_match.description: A text, binary, file name, or datastore that matched against a detection rule.

policy.description: Details about the policy that triggered the finding.

src_url.description: The source URL pointing towards the full classification job details.

status.description: The resultant status of the classification job normalized to the caption of the status_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

status_details.description: The contextual description of the status, status_id value.

anyOf.description: The status is unknown.
The classification job completed for the evaluated resource.
The classification job partially completed for the evaluated resource.
The classification job failed for the evaluated resource.
The classification job type id is not mapped.

status_id.description: The normalized status identifier of the classification job.

total.description: The total count of discovered entities, by the classification job.

uid.description: The unique identifier of the classification job.

OcsfDataSecurity.title: OcsfDataSecurity

OcsfDataSecurityFinding.description:
A Data Security Finding describes detections or alerts generated by various data security products such as Data Loss Prevention (DLP), Data Classification, Secrets Management, Digital Rights Management (DRM), Data Security Posture Management (DSPM), and similar tools. These detections or alerts can be created using fingerprinting, statistical analysis, machine learning or other methodologies. The finding describes the actors and endpoints who accessed or own the sensitive data, as well as the resources which store the sensitive data. Note: if the event producer is a security control, the security_control profile should be applied and its attacks information, if present, should be duplicated into the finding_info object.
Note: If the Finding is an incident, i.e. requires incident workflow, also apply the incident profile or aggregate this finding into an Incident Finding.

anyOf.description: The action was unknown. The disposition_id attribute may still be set to a non-unknown value, for example 'Custom Action', 'Challenge'.
The activity was allowed. The disposition_id attribute should be set to a value that conforms to this action, for example 'Allowed', 'Approved', 'Delayed', 'No Action', 'Count' etc.

The attempted activity was denied. The disposition_id attribute should be set to a value that conforms to this action, for example 'Blocked', 'Rejected', 'Quarantined', 'Isolated', 'Dropped', 'Access Revoked, etc.

The activity was observed, but neither explicitly allowed nor denied. This is common with IDS and EDR controls that report additional information on observed behavior such as TTPs. The disposition_id attribute should be set to a value that conforms to this action, for example 'Logged', 'Alert', 'Detected', 'Count', etc.
The activity was modified, adjusted, or corrected. The disposition_id attribute should be set appropriately, for example 'Restored', 'Corrected', 'Delayed', 'Captcha', 'Tagged'.
The action is not mapped. See the action attribute which contains a data source specific value.

action_id.description: The action taken by a control or other policy-based system leading to an outcome or disposition. An unknown action may still correspond to a known disposition. Refer to disposition_id for the outcome of the action.

anyOf.description: The event activity is unknown.
A new Data Security finding is created.
An existing Data Security finding is updated with more information.
An existing Data Security finding is closed, this can be due to any resolution (e.g., True Positive, False Positive, etc.).
An existing Data Security finding is suppressed due to inaccurate detection techniques or a known true negative.
The event activity is not mapped. See the activity_name attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

activity_id.description: The normalized identifier of the Data Security Finding activity.

activity_name.description: The Data Security finding activity name, as defined by the activity_id.

actor.description: Describes details about the actor implicated in the data security finding. Either an actor that owns a particular digital file or information store, or an actor which accessed classified or sensitive data.

api.description: Describes details about a typical API (Application Programming Interface) call.

assignee.description: The details of the user assigned to an Incident.

assignee_group.description: The details of the group assigned to an Incident.

attacks.description: An array of MITRE ATT&CK® objects describing identified tactics, techniques & sub-techniques. The objects are compatible with MITRE ATLAS™ tactics, techniques & sub-techniques.

attestation_list.description: One or more cryptographic attestation objects over an event, each providing integrity, authenticity, and non-repudiation. Independent attesters over the same event — for example a producer at write time and a downstream processor at ingest — each contribute a separate attestation, distinct from co-signers on a single attestation, which share its signatures array. Carried on the record_integrity profile; the object itself is domain-agnostic.

authorizations.description: Provides details about an authorization, such as authorization outcome, and any associated policies related to the activity/event.

category_name.description: The event category name, as defined by category_uid value: Findings.

category_uid.description: The category unique identifier of the event. Each event class belongs to exactly one category. Producers and mappers must set this to the category defined by the event class being used.

class_name.description: The event class name, as defined by class_uid value: Data Security Finding.

class_uid.description: The unique identifier of a class. A class describes the attributes available in an event. Producers and mappers must set this to the uid defined in the event class definition. For example, Detection Finding is 2004.

cloud.description: Describes details about the Cloud environment where the event or finding was created.

comment.description: A user provided comment about the finding.

confidence.description: The confidence, normalized to the caption of the confidence_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source and should be the same as confidence_score if also populated..

anyOf.description: The normalized confidence is unknown.
The confidence is not mapped to the defined enum values. See the confidence attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

confidence_id.description: The normalized confidence refers to the accuracy of the analytics that produced the finding. An analytic with a low confidence means that the finding scope is wide and may create finding reports that are noisy or may not be malicious in nature.

confidence_score.description: The confidence score as reported by the event source. If confidence_id is 99 'Other', it should be the same as confidence if both are populated.

count.description: The number of events aggregated into this single record. Only populate for aggregate events. When set, start_time and end_time should also be provided to define the aggregation window.

data_security.description: The Data Security object describes the characteristics, techniques and content of a Data Loss Prevention (DLP), Data Loss Detection (DLD), Data Classification, or similar tools' finding, alert, or detection mechanism(s).

database.description: Describes the database where classified or sensitive data is stored in, or was accessed from. Databases are typically datastore services that contain an organized collection of structured and/or semi-structured data.

databucket.description: Describes the databucket where classified or sensitive data is stored in, or was accessed from. The data bucket object is a basic container that holds data, typically organized through the use of data partitions.

device.description: Describes the device where classified or sensitive data is stored in, or was accessed from.

disposition.description: The disposition name, normalized to the caption of the disposition_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

anyOf.description: The disposition is unknown.
Granted access or allowed the action to the protected resource.
Denied access or blocked the action to the protected resource.
A suspicious file or other content was moved to a benign location.
A session was isolated on the network or within a browser.
A file or other content was deleted.
The request was detected as a threat and resulted in the connection being dropped.
A custom action was executed such as running of a command script. Use the message attribute of the base class for details.
A request or submission was approved. For example, when a form was properly filled out and submitted. This is distinct from 1 'Allowed'.
A quarantined file or other content was restored to its original location.
A suspicious or risky entity was deemed to no longer be suspicious (re-scored).
A corrupt file or configuration was corrected.
A corrupt file or configuration was partially corrected.
A corrupt file or configuration was not corrected.
An operation was delayed, for example if a restart was required to finish the operation.
Suspicious activity or a policy violation was detected without further action.
The outcome of an operation had no action taken.
The operation or action was logged without further action.
A file or other entity was marked with extended attributes.
The request or activity was detected as a threat and resulted in a notification but request was not blocked.
Counted the request or activity but did not determine whether to allow it or block it.
The request was detected as a threat and resulted in the connection being reset.
Required the end user to solve a CAPTCHA puzzle to prove that a human being is sending the request.
Ran a silent challenge that required the client session to verify that it's a browser, and not a bot.
The requestor's access has been revoked due to security policy enforcements. Note: use the Host profile if the User or Actor requestor is not present in the event class.
A request or submission was rejected. For example, when a form was improperly filled out and submitted. This is distinct from 2 'Blocked'.

An attempt to access a resource was denied due to an authorization check that failed. This is a more specific disposition than 2 'Blocked' and can be complemented with the authorizations attribute for more detail.
An error occurred during the processing of the activity or request. Use the message attribute of the base class for details.
The disposition is not mapped. See the disposition attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

disposition_id.description: Describes the outcome or action taken by a security control, such as access control checks, malware detections or various types of policy violations.

dst_endpoint.description: Describes the endpoint where classified or sensitive data is stored in, or was accessed from.

duration.description: The elapsed time of the aggregation window in milliseconds, from start_time to end_time. Only populate for aggregate events (count > 1). The value should equal end_time - start_time.

end_time.description: The time of the most recent event or finding that contributed to this finding.

end_time_dt.description: The time of the most recent event or finding that contributed to this finding.

enrichments.description:
The additional information from an external data source, which is associated with the event or a finding. For example add location information for the IP address in the DNS answers:

[{"name": "answers.ip", "value": "92.24.47.250", "type": "location", "data": {"city": "Socotra", "continent": "Asia", "coordinates": [-25.4153, 17.0743], "country": "YE", "desc": "Yemen"}}]

file.description: Describes a file that contains classified or sensitive data.

finding_info.description: Describes the supporting information about a generated finding.

firewall_rule.description: The firewall rule that pertains to the control that triggered the event, if applicable.

impact.description: The impact , normalized to the caption of the impact_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

anyOf.description: The normalized impact is unknown.
The magnitude of harm is low.
The magnitude of harm is moderate.
The magnitude of harm is high.
The magnitude of harm is high and the scope is widespread.
The impact is not mapped. See the impact attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

impact_id.description: The normalized impact of the incident or finding. Per NIST, this is the magnitude of harm that can be expected to result from the consequences of unauthorized disclosure, modification, destruction, or loss of information or information system availability.

impact_score.description: The impact as an integer value of the finding, valid range 0-100.

is_alert.description: Indicates that the event is considered to be an alertable signal. For example, an activity_id of 'Create' could constitute an alertable signal and the value would be true, while 'Close' likely would not and either omit the attribute or set its value to false. Note that other events with the security_control profile may also be deemed alertable signals and may also carry is_alert = true attributes.

is_suspected_breach.description: A determination based on analytics as to whether a potential breach was found.

malware.description: A list of Malware objects, describing details about the identified malware.

malware_scan_info.description: Describes details about the scan job that identified malware on the target system.

message.description: A human-readable description of the event, as defined by the source. This should be a concise, meaningful summary suitable for display in a UI or alert notification - not a raw log line. For example: "User john_doe logged in from 10.0.0.1." rather than a raw syslog string.

metadata.description: The metadata object describes the event producer, schema version, and processing information. Producers and mappers must populate metadata.product to identify the data source, and metadata.version to indicate the OCSF schema version used. Consumers rely on this to interpret the event correctly.

notes.description: Additional notes related to the finding. Each note in the array can include a comment, the user who made the comment, the time when the note was created, and the time when the note was last modified (typically by the same user). Notes can be used to provide additional context, explanations, or observations by analysts related to the finding over time.

observables.description: The observables array surfaces key indicators and entities from the event or finding in a single, consistent location for downstream correlation and detection. Each entry references an attribute path within the event (e.g., src_endpoint.ip) along with its type and value, enabling consumers to extract IOCs without parsing the full event structure.

osint.description: The OSINT (Open Source Intelligence) object contains details related to an indicator such as the indicator itself, related indicators, geolocation, registrar information, subdomains, analyst commentary, and other contextual information. This information can be used to further enrich a detection or finding by providing decisioning support to other analysts and engineers.

policy.description: The policy that pertains to the control that triggered the event, if applicable. For example the name of an anti-malware policy or an access control policy.

priority.description: The priority, normalized to the caption of the priority_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

anyOf.description: No priority is assigned.
Application or personal procedure is unusable, where a workaround is available or a repair is possible.
Non-critical function or procedure is unusable or hard to use causing operational disruptions with no direct impact on a service's availability. A workaround is available.
Critical functionality or network access is interrupted, degraded or unusable, having a severe impact on services availability. No acceptable alternative is possible.
Interruption making a critical functionality inaccessible or a complete network interruption causing a severe impact on services availability. There is no possible alternative.
The priority is not normalized.

priority_id.description: The normalized priority. Priority identifies the relative importance of the incident or finding. It is a measurement of urgency.

raw_data.description: The original event/finding data as received from the source, before normalization into OCSF. Populate this with the verbatim log line, JSON payload, or other native format for forensic and debugging purposes. This field is not intended for structured querying - use the normalized OCSF attributes instead.

raw_data_hash.description: A fingerprint (hash) of the raw_data content. Use this to verify the integrity of the original event data or to deduplicate events.

raw_data_size.description: The size of the original event data (as captured in raw_data) in bytes, before OCSF normalization. Useful for metering and capacity planning.

resources.description:
Describes details about additional resources, where classified or sensitive data is stored in, or was accessed from.

You can populate this object, if the specific resource type objects available in the class (database, databucket, table, file) aren't sufficient; OR
You can also choose to duplicate uid, name of the specific resources objects, for a consistent access to resource uids across all findings.

risk_details.description: Describes the risk associated with the finding.

risk_level.description: The risk level, normalized to the caption of the risk_level_id value.

anyOf.description: The risk level is not mapped. See the risk_level attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

risk_score.description: The risk score as reported by the event source.

severity.description: The event/finding severity label, normalized to the caption of the severity_id value. When severity_id is 99 (Other), this attribute must contain the source-specific severity label. For all other values, this should match the caption defined for that severity_id enum value (e.g., "High" for severity_id: 4).

anyOf.description: The event/finding severity is unknown.
Informational message. No action required.
The user decides if action is needed.
Action is required but the situation is not serious at this time.
Action is required immediately.
Action is required immediately and the scope is broad.
An error occurred but it is too late to take remedial action.
The event/finding severity is not mapped. See the severity attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

severity_id.description:
The normalized identifier of the event/finding severity.

The normalized severity is a measurement the effort and expense required to manage and resolve an event or incident. Smaller numerical values represent lower impact events, and larger numerical values represent higher impact events.

src_endpoint.description: Details about the source endpoint where classified or sensitive data was accessed from.

src_url.description: A Url link used to access the original incident.

start_time.description: The time of the earliest event or finding that contributed to this finding.

start_time_dt.description: The time of the earliest event or finding that contributed to this finding.

status.description: The finding lifecycle status label, normalized to the caption of the status_id value. When status_id is 99 (Other), this must contain the source-specific status label.

status_code.description: The source-specific status or error code as reported by the event source. For example, a Windows logon failure code (0x18), an HTTP response code (403), or an AWS API error code. This preserves the original code for detailed troubleshooting beyond what status_id conveys.

status_detail.description: A human-readable description providing additional context about the event outcome. Use this to convey details that go beyond the normalized status_id and source-specific status_code, such as a failure reason or error message. For example: "Account locked after 5 failed attempts.".

anyOf.description: The status is unknown.
The Finding is new and yet to be reviewed.
The Finding is under review.
The Finding was reviewed, determined to be benign or a false positive and is now suppressed.
The Finding was reviewed, remediated and is now considered resolved.
The Finding was archived.
The Finding was deleted. For example, it might have been created in error.
The status is not mapped. See the status attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

status_id.description: The normalized finding lifecycle status identifier. Unlike the status of an activity event, which indicates the success or failure of the activity, finding status tracks the review and triage workflow: whether the finding is new, being investigated, suppressed, or resolved. Producers should set this to reflect the current state of the finding in their system (e.g., 1 for newly created findings, 4 when remediated).

table.description: Describes the table where classified or sensitive data is stored in, or was accessed from. The table object represents a table within a structured relational database, warehouse, lake, or similar.

ticket.description: The linked ticket in the ticketing system.

tickets.description: The associated ticket(s) in the ticketing system. Each ticket contains details like ticket ID, status, etc.

time.description: The finding creation time - when the finding was first generated, not when the underlying activity occurred. For the time range of contributing events, use start_time and end_time.

time_dt.description: The finding creation time - when the finding was first generated, not when the underlying activity occurred. For the time range of contributing events, use start_time and end_time.

timezone_offset.description: The number of minutes that the reported event time is ahead or behind UTC, in the range -1,080 to +1,080. This allows consumers to reconstruct the local time at the event source. For example, US Eastern Standard Time is -300. Populate this when the source provides local time zone information.

type_name.description: The event/finding type name, combining the class and activity (e.g., "Detection Finding: Create"). The value must match the class_name and activity_name joined by ": ".

anyOf.description: A new Data Security finding is created.
An existing Data Security finding is updated with more information.
An existing Data Security finding is closed, this can be due to any resolution (e.g., True Positive, False Positive, etc.).
An existing Data Security finding is suppressed due to inaccurate detection techniques or a known true negative.

type_uid.description: The event/finding type ID. It identifies the event's semantics and structure. Producers and mappers must compute this as class_uid * 100 + activity_id. It uniquely identifies the combination of event class and activity across the entire schema. For example, Detection Finding: Create is 200401.

unmapped.description:
A container for source-specific attributes that do not map to any defined OCSF attribute. Use this to preserve valuable source data that would otherwise be lost during normalization. The keys and values are specific to the event source.

Note: Consumers should not rely on a stable structure within this field. The preferred approach to unmapped attributes is to create a custom extension with the desired structure.

vendor_attributes.description:
The Vendor Attributes object can be used to represent values of attributes populated by the Vendor/Finding Provider. It can help distinguish between the vendor-provided values and consumer-updated values, of key attributes like severity_id.
The original finding producer should not populate this object. It should be populated by consuming systems that support data mutability.

verdict.description: The verdict assigned to an Incident finding.

anyOf.description: The type is unknown.
The incident is a false positive.
The incident is a true positive.
The incident can be disregarded as it is unimportant, an error or accident.
The incident is suspicious.
The incident is benign.
The incident is a test.
The incident has insufficient data to make a verdict.
The incident is a security risk.
The incident remediation or required actions are managed externally.
The incident is a duplicate.
The type is not mapped. See the type attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

verdict_id.description: The normalized verdict of an Incident.

OcsfDataSecurityFinding.title: OcsfDataSecurityFinding

OcsfDatabase.description: The database object is used for databases which are typically datastore services that contain an organized collection of structured and unstructured data or a types of data.

created_time.description: The time when the database was known to have been created.

created_time_dt.description: The time when the database was known to have been created.

data_classification.description: The Data Classification object includes information about data classification levels and data category types.

data_classifications.description: A list of Data Classification objects, that include information about data classification levels and data category types, identified by a classifier.

desc.description: The description of the database.

embedding_model.description: Model used for creating embeddings (if applicable). For example: text-embedding-ada-002 or all-MiniLM-L6-v2.

groups.description: The group names to which the database belongs.

modified_time.description: The most recent time when any changes, updates, or modifications were made within the database.

modified_time_dt.description: The most recent time when any changes, updates, or modifications were made within the database.

name.description: The database name, ordinarily as assigned by a database administrator.

size.description: The size of the database in bytes.

type.description: The database type.

anyOf.description: The type is unknown.
The type is not mapped. See the type attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

type_id.description: The normalized identifier of the database type.

uid.description: The unique identifier of the database.

uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

OcsfDatabase.title: OcsfDatabase

OcsfDatabucket.description: The databucket object is a basic container that holds data, typically organized through the use of data partitions.

agent_list.description: A list of agent objects associated with a device, endpoint, or resource.

cloud_partition.description: The logical grouping or isolated segment within a cloud provider's infrastructure where the databucket is located.

created_time.description: The time when the databucket was known to have been created.

created_time_dt.description: The time when the databucket was known to have been created.

criticality.description: The criticality of the databucket as defined by the event source.

data_classification.description: The Data Classification object includes information about data classification levels and data category types.

data_classifications.description: A list of Data Classification objects, that include information about data classification levels and data category types, identified by a classifier.

desc.description: The description of the databucket.

encryption_details.description: The encryption details of the databucket. Should be populated if the databucket is encrypted.

file.description: Details about the file/object within a databucket.

group.description: The name of the related resource group.

groups.description: The group names to which the databucket belongs.

hostname.description: The fully qualified hostname of the databucket.

ip.description: The IP address of the resource, in either IPv4 or IPv6 format.

is_backed_up.description: Indicates whether the device or resource has a backup enabled, such as an automated snapshot or a cloud backup. For example, this is indicated by the cloudBackupEnabled value within JAMF Pro mobile devices or the registration of an AWS ARN with the AWS Backup service.

is_encrypted.description: Indicates if the databucket is encrypted.

is_public.description: Indicates if the databucket is publicly accessible.

labels.description: The list of labels associated to the resource.

modified_time.description: The most recent time when any changes, updates, or modifications were made within the databucket.

modified_time_dt.description: The most recent time when any changes, updates, or modifications were made within the databucket.

name.description: The databucket name.

namespace.description: The namespace is useful when similar entities exist that you need to keep separate.

owner.description: The identity of the service or user account that owns the databucket.

region.description: The cloud region of the databucket.

resource_relationship.description: A graph representation showing how this databucket relates to and interacts with other entities in the environment. This can include parent/child relationships, dependencies, or other connections.

size.description: The size of the databucket in bytes.

tags.description: The list of tags; {key:value} pairs associated to the resource.

type.description: The databucket type.

anyOf.description: The type is unknown.
The type is not mapped. See the type attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

type_id.description: The normalized identifier of the databucket type.

uid.description: The unique identifier of the databucket.

uid_alt.description: The alternative unique identifier of the resource.

uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

version.description: The version of the resource. For example 1.2.3.

zone.description: The specific availability zone within a cloud region where the databucket is located.

OcsfDatastoreActivity.description: Datastore events describe general activities (Read, Update, Query, Delete, etc.) which affect datastores or data within those datastores, e.g. (AWS RDS, AWS S3).

anyOf.description: The action was unknown. The disposition_id attribute may still be set to a non-unknown value, for example 'Custom Action', 'Challenge'.
The activity was allowed. The disposition_id attribute should be set to a value that conforms to this action, for example 'Allowed', 'Approved', 'Delayed', 'No Action', 'Count' etc.

The attempted activity was denied. The disposition_id attribute should be set to a value that conforms to this action, for example 'Blocked', 'Rejected', 'Quarantined', 'Isolated', 'Dropped', 'Access Revoked, etc.

The activity was observed, but neither explicitly allowed nor denied. This is common with IDS and EDR controls that report additional information on observed behavior such as TTPs. The disposition_id attribute should be set to a value that conforms to this action, for example 'Logged', 'Alert', 'Detected', 'Count', etc.
The activity was modified, adjusted, or corrected. The disposition_id attribute should be set appropriately, for example 'Restored', 'Corrected', 'Delayed', 'Captcha', 'Tagged'.
The action is not mapped. See the action attribute which contains a data source specific value.

action_id.description: The action taken by a control or other policy-based system leading to an outcome or disposition. An unknown action may still correspond to a known disposition. Refer to disposition_id for the outcome of the action.

anyOf.description: The event activity is unknown.
The 'Read' activity involves accessing specific data record details.
The 'Update' activity pertains to modifying specific data record details.
The 'Connect' activity involves establishing a connection to the datastore.
The 'Query' activity involves retrieving a filtered subset of data based on specific criteria.
The 'Write' activity involves writing specific data record details.
The 'Create' activity involves generating new data record details.
The 'Delete' activity involves removing specific data record details.
The 'List' activity provides an overview of existing data records.
The 'Encrypt' activity involves securing data by encrypting a specific data record.
The 'Decrypt' activity involves converting encrypted data back to its original format.
The event activity is not mapped. See the activity_name attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

activity_id.description: The normalized identifier of the activity that triggered the event. Each event class defines its own set of activity values. Use 0 (Unknown) when the activity cannot be determined. Use 99 (Other) when the activity does not match any defined value, in which case activity_name must be populated with the source-specific label.

activity_name.description: The event activity name, as defined by the activity_id. When activity_id is 99 (Other), this attribute must contain the source-specific activity label. For all other activity_id values, this must match the caption defined for that activity_id enum value.

actor.description: The user, process, or service that initiated the activity on the host. For system-level events this is typically a process; for IAM events it is typically a user or role.

ai_agent.description: The autonomous AI agent that performed this operation. Carries model identity via ai_agent.ai_model. Populate when the action was performed by an agent rather than a direct model call.

ai_model.description: The AI model involved in this operation. Use for direct model invocations where no autonomous agent is involved. For agent-mediated operations, model identity is carried within ai_agent.ai_model instead.

api.description: Describes details about a typical API (Application Programming Interface) call.

attacks.description: An array of MITRE ATT&CK® objects describing identified tactics, techniques & sub-techniques. The objects are compatible with MITRE ATLAS™ tactics, techniques & sub-techniques.

attestation_list.description: One or more cryptographic attestation objects over an event, each providing integrity, authenticity, and non-repudiation. Independent attesters over the same event — for example a producer at write time and a downstream processor at ingest — each contribute a separate attestation, distinct from co-signers on a single attestation, which share its signatures array. Carried on the record_integrity profile; the object itself is domain-agnostic.

authorizations.description: Provides details about an authorization, such as authorization outcome, and any associated policies related to the activity/event.

category_name.description: The event category name, as defined by category_uid value: Application Activity.

category_uid.description: The category unique identifier of the event. Each event class belongs to exactly one category. Producers and mappers must set this to the category defined by the event class being used.

class_name.description: The event class name, as defined by class_uid value: Datastore Activity.

class_uid.description: The unique identifier of a class. A class describes the attributes available in an event. Producers and mappers must set this to the uid defined in the event class definition. For example, Detection Finding is 2004.

cloud.description: Describes details about the Cloud environment where the event or finding was created.

confidence.description: The confidence, normalized to the caption of the confidence_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

anyOf.description: The normalized confidence is unknown.
The confidence is not mapped to the defined enum values. See the confidence attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

confidence_id.description: The normalized confidence refers to the accuracy of the security control or alert. An analytic with a low confidence means that the alerts may be noisy or may not be malicious in nature.

confidence_score.description: The confidence score as reported by the event source. If confidence_id is 99 'Other', it should be the same as confidence if both are populated.

count.description: The number of events aggregated into this single record. Only populate for aggregate events. When set, start_time and end_time should also be provided to define the aggregation window.

database.description: The database object is used for databases which are typically datastore services that contain an organized collection of structured and unstructured data or a types of data.

databucket.description: The data bucket object is a basic container that holds data, typically organized through the use of data partitions.

delegation.description: The delegation under whose authority this AI operation was performed. Links the event to a durable authorization context independent of traces and sessions, enabling correlation of all events executed under the same delegated authority.

device.description: The host or device where the activity was observed. Populate with details such as hostname, IP address, OS, and hardware identifiers when available from the source.

disposition.description: The disposition name, normalized to the caption of the disposition_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

Granted access or allowed the action to the protected resource.
Denied access or blocked the action to the protected resource.

The request was detected as a threat and resulted in the connection being reset.
Required the end user to solve a CAPTCHA puzzle to prove that a human being is sending the request.
Ran a silent challenge that required the client session to verify that it's a browser, and not a bot.
The requestor's access has been revoked due to security policy enforcements. Note: use the Host profile if the User or Actor requestor is not present in the event class.
A request or submission was rejected. For example, when a form was improperly filled out and submitted. This is distinct from 2 'Blocked'.

An attempt to access a resource was denied due to an authorization check that failed. This is a more specific disposition than 2 'Blocked' and can be complemented with the authorizations attribute for more detail.
An error occurred during the processing of the activity or request. Use the message attribute of the base class for details.

disposition_id.description: Describes the outcome or action taken by a security control, such as access control checks, malware detections or various types of policy violations.

dst_endpoint.description: Details about the endpoint hosting the datastore application or service.
