The disposition is not mapped. See the disposition attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

disposition_id.description: Describes the outcome or action taken by a security control, such as access control checks, malware detections or various types of policy violations.

dst_endpoint.description: The responder (server) of the DHCP connection.

duration.description: The elapsed time of the aggregation window in milliseconds, from start_time to end_time. Only populate for aggregate events (count > 1). The value should equal end_time - start_time.

end_time.description: The time of the most recent event in an aggregate (count > 1). Do not populate for discrete, point-in-time events - use time alone. Subclasses such as findings may redefine this for their own time-range semantics.

end_time_dt.description: The time of the most recent event in an aggregate (count > 1). Do not populate for discrete, point-in-time events - use time alone. Subclasses such as findings may redefine this for their own time-range semantics.

enrichments.description:
The additional information from an external data source, which is associated with the event or a finding. For example add location information for the IP address in the DNS answers:

[{"name": "answers.ip", "value": "92.24.47.250", "type": "location", "data": {"city": "Socotra", "continent": "Asia", "coordinates": [-25.4153, 17.0743], "country": "YE", "desc": "Yemen"}}]

firewall_rule.description: The firewall rule that pertains to the control that triggered the event, if applicable.

is_alert.description: Indicates that the event is considered to be an alertable signal. Should be set to true if disposition_id = Alert among other dispositions, and/or risk_level_id or severity_id of the event is elevated. Not all control events will be alertable, for example if disposition_id = Exonerated or disposition_id = Allowed.

is_renewal.description: Indicates whether this is a lease/session renewal event.

ja4_fingerprint_list.description: A list of the JA4+ network fingerprints.

lease_dur.description: This represents the length of the DHCP lease in seconds. This is present in DHCP Ack events.

load_balancer.description: The Load Balancer object contains information related to the device that is distributing incoming traffic to specified destinations.

malware.description: A list of Malware objects, describing details about the identified malware.

malware_scan_info.description: Describes details about the scan job that identified malware on the target system.

message.description: A human-readable description of the event, as defined by the source. This should be a concise, meaningful summary suitable for display in a UI or alert notification - not a raw log line. For example: "User john_doe logged in from 10.0.0.1." rather than a raw syslog string.

message_context.description: Communication context for AI system interactions including protocols, roles, clients, and session information for MCP and other AI communication systems.

metadata.description: The metadata object describes the event producer, schema version, and processing information. Producers and mappers must populate metadata.product to identify the data source, and metadata.version to indicate the OCSF schema version used. Consumers rely on this to interpret the event correctly.

network_observation_point.description: The network endpoint that observes or inspects network traffic as a third-party system, used when the observer is neither the source nor the destination of the communication (when observation_point_id = 3). Examples include network taps, span ports, inline security devices, or packet capture systems that monitor traffic between other endpoints.

observables.description: The observables array surfaces key indicators and entities from the event or finding in a single, consistent location for downstream correlation and detection. Each entry references an attribute path within the event (e.g., src_endpoint.ip) along with its type and value, enabling consumers to extract IOCs without parsing the full event structure.

observation_point.description: Indicates whether the source network endpoint, destination network endpoint, or neither served as the observation point for the activity. The value is normalized to the caption of the observation_point_id.

anyOf.description: The observation point is unknown.
The source network endpoint is the observation point.
The destination network endpoint is the observation point.
Neither the source nor destination network endpoint is the observation point. Refer to the network_observation_point attribute for details.

Both the source and destination network endpoint are the observation point. This typically occurs in localhost or internal communications where the source and destination are the same endpoint, often resulting in a connection_info.direction of Local.
The observation point is not mapped. See the observation_point attribute for a data source specific value.

observation_point_id.description: The normalized identifier of the observation point. The observation point identifier indicates whether the source network endpoint, destination network endpoint, or neither served as the observation point for the activity.

osint.description: The OSINT (Open Source Intelligence) object contains details related to an indicator such as the indicator itself, related indicators, geolocation, registrar information, subdomains, analyst commentary, and other contextual information. This information can be used to further enrich a detection or finding by providing decisioning support to other analysts and engineers.

packet_list.description: The list of packet objects describing captured network packets.

policy.description: The policy that pertains to the control that triggered the event, if applicable. For example the name of an anti-malware policy or an access control policy.

proxy.description: The proxy (server) in a network connection.

proxy_connection_info.description: The connection information from the proxy server to the remote server.

proxy_endpoint.description: The proxy (server) in a network connection.

proxy_http_request.description: The HTTP Request from the proxy server to the remote server.

proxy_http_response.description: The HTTP Response from the remote server to the proxy server.

proxy_tls.description: The TLS protocol negotiated between the proxy server and the remote server.

proxy_traffic.description: The network traffic refers to the amount of data moving across a network, from proxy to remote server at a given point of time.

raw_data.description: The original event/finding data as received from the source, before normalization into OCSF. Populate this with the verbatim log line, JSON payload, or other native format for forensic and debugging purposes. This field is not intended for structured querying - use the normalized OCSF attributes instead.

raw_data_hash.description: A fingerprint (hash) of the raw_data content. Use this to verify the integrity of the original event data or to deduplicate events.

raw_data_size.description: The size of the original event data (as captured in raw_data) in bytes, before OCSF normalization. Useful for metering and capacity planning.

relay.description: The network relay that is associated with the event.

risk_details.description: Describes the risk associated with the finding.

risk_level.description: The risk level, normalized to the caption of the risk_level_id value.

anyOf.description: The risk level is not mapped. See the risk_level attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

risk_score.description: The risk score as reported by the event source.

severity.description: The event/finding severity label, normalized to the caption of the severity_id value. When severity_id is 99 (Other), this attribute must contain the source-specific severity label. For all other values, this should match the caption defined for that severity_id enum value (e.g., "High" for severity_id: 4).

anyOf.description: The event/finding severity is unknown.
Informational message. No action required.
The user decides if action is needed.
Action is required but the situation is not serious at this time.
Action is required immediately.
Action is required immediately and the scope is broad.
An error occurred but it is too late to take remedial action.
The event/finding severity is not mapped. See the severity attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

severity_id.description:
The normalized identifier of the event/finding severity.

The normalized severity is a measurement the effort and expense required to manage and resolve an event or incident. Smaller numerical values represent lower impact events, and larger numerical values represent higher impact events.

src_endpoint.description: The initiator (client) of the DHCP connection.

start_time.description: The time of the earliest event in an aggregate (count > 1). Do not populate for discrete, point-in-time events - use time alone. Subclasses such as findings may redefine this for their own time-range semantics.

start_time_dt.description: The time of the earliest event in an aggregate (count > 1). Do not populate for discrete, point-in-time events - use time alone. Subclasses such as findings may redefine this for their own time-range semantics.

status.description: The event status label, normalized to the caption of the status_id value. When status_id is 99 (Other), this attribute must contain the source-specific status label. For all other values, this must match the caption defined for that status_id enum value (e.g., "Success" for status_id: 1).

status_code.description: The source-specific status or error code as reported by the event source. For example, a Windows logon failure code (0x18), an HTTP response code (403), or an AWS API error code. This preserves the original code for detailed troubleshooting beyond what status_id conveys.

status_detail.description: A human-readable description providing additional context about the event outcome. Use this to convey details that go beyond the normalized status_id and source-specific status_code, such as a failure reason or error message. For example: "Account locked after 5 failed attempts.".

anyOf.description: The status is unknown.
The activity completed successfully.
The activity failed.
The status is not mapped. See the status attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

status_id.description: The normalized status of the event outcome. Use this family of attributes to convey the outcome of the activity described by the event. Producers should map their source outcome to 1 (Success) or 2 (Failure). Use 0 (Unknown) when the outcome cannot be determined, and 99 (Other) with a populated status string when the source value does not map cleanly.

time.description: The primary timestamp of the event - when the activity actually occurred at the source. This does not capture when the event record was created or serialized by the source system; for event lifecycle timestamps such as ingestion and processing, use metadata.logged_time and metadata.processed_time respectively, or the equivalent attributes in the metadata.loggers array when recording pipeline stages. For aggregate events (count > 1), set this to start_time (the earliest OCSF time in the aggregate) to preserve causal ordering and consistent timeline alignment. Note: finding classes redefine time as the finding creation time rather than the activity occurrence time. This must be a UTC epoch value in milliseconds (e.g., 1776881335332). Mappers should use the most precise and authoritative timestamp available from the source.

time_dt.description: The primary timestamp of the event - when the activity actually occurred at the source. This does not capture when the event record was created or serialized by the source system; for event lifecycle timestamps such as ingestion and processing, use metadata.logged_time and metadata.processed_time respectively, or the equivalent attributes in the metadata.loggers array when recording pipeline stages. For aggregate events (count > 1), set this to start_time (the earliest OCSF time in the aggregate) to preserve causal ordering and consistent timeline alignment. Note: finding classes redefine time as the finding creation time rather than the activity occurrence time. This must be a UTC epoch value in milliseconds (e.g., 1776881335332). Mappers should use the most precise and authoritative timestamp available from the source.

timezone_offset.description: The number of minutes that the reported event time is ahead or behind UTC, in the range -1,080 to +1,080. This allows consumers to reconstruct the local time at the event source. For example, US Eastern Standard Time is -300. Populate this when the source provides local time zone information.

traffic.description: The network traffic for this observation period. Use when reporting: (1) delta values (bytes/packets transferred since the last observation), (2) instantaneous measurements at a specific point in time, or (3) standalone single-event metrics. This attribute represents a point-in-time measurement or incremental change, not a running total. For accumulated totals across multiple observations or the lifetime of a flow, use cumulative_traffic instead.

transaction_uid.description: The unique identifier of the transaction. This is typically a random number generated from the client to associate a dhcp request/response pair.

type_name.description: The event/finding type name, combining the class and activity (e.g., "Detection Finding: Create"). The value must match the class_name and activity_name joined by ": ".

anyOf.description: DHCPDISCOVER
DHCPOFFER
DHCPREQUEST
DHCPDECLINE
DHCPACK: The server accepts the request by sending the client a DHCP Acknowledgment message.
DHCPNAK
DHCPRELEASE: A DHCP client sends a DHCPRELEASE packet to the server to release the IP address and cancel any remaining lease.
DHCPINFORM
DHCPEXPIRE: A DHCP lease expired.

type_uid.description: The event/finding type ID. It identifies the event's semantics and structure. Producers and mappers must compute this as class_uid * 100 + activity_id. It uniquely identifies the combination of event class and activity across the entire schema. For example, Detection Finding: Create is 200401.

unmapped.description:
A container for source-specific attributes that do not map to any defined OCSF attribute. Use this to preserve valuable source data that would otherwise be lost during normalization. The keys and values are specific to the event source.

Note: Consumers should not rely on a stable structure within this field. The preferred approach to unmapped attributes is to create a custom extension with the desired structure.

OcsfDhcpActivity.title: OcsfDhcpActivity

OcsfDigitalSignature.description: The Digital Signature object contains information about the cryptographic mechanism used to verify the authenticity, integrity, and origin of the file or application.

algorithm.description: The digital signature algorithm used to create the signature, normalized to the caption of 'algorithm_id'. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

anyOf.description: The algorithm is unknown.
Digital Signature Algorithm (DSA).
Rivest-Shamir-Adleman (RSA) Algorithm.
Elliptic Curve Digital Signature Algorithm.
Authenticode Digital Signature Algorithm.
Code Signing Algorithm.
Application Package Signing Algorithm.
The algorithm is not mapped. See the algorithm attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

algorithm_id.description: The identifier of the normalized digital signature algorithm.

certificate.description: The certificate object containing information about the digital certificate.

created_time.description: The time when the digital signature was created.

created_time_dt.description: The time when the digital signature was created.

developer_uid.description: The developer ID on the certificate that signed the file.

digest.description: The message digest attribute contains the fixed length message hash representation and the corresponding hashing algorithm information.

serialization.description: The canonical serialization or signing-envelope scheme used to produce the deterministic byte sequence that was signed, normalized to the caption of serialization_id. In the case of Other, it is defined by the event source.

anyOf.description: No canonical serialization or signing envelope was applied; the signature is computed over the data's raw byte sequence, such as the content of a disk file or any other opaque byte stream.
JSON Canonicalization Scheme - deterministic JSON serialization of the structured data prior to signing.
JSON Web Signature - the JWS Signing Input, i.e. BASE64URL(protected header) '.' BASE64URL(payload).
CBOR Object Signing and Encryption - the CBOR Sig_structure used as the binary signing input.

Dead Simple Signing Envelope - the PAE (Pre-Authentication Encoding) canonical signing input. Note: DSSE is a signing-envelope scheme, not a hash algorithm; any payload hash is carried separately in the fingerprint object.

The Portable Executable (PE) Image Hash procedure that canonicalizes the PE structure into the byte sequence fed to the digest, excluding specified header fields and digesting sections in a defined order. Authenticode bundles canonicalization and signing format: when used, algorithm_id is also set to the Authenticode enum value.
The procedure that describes how hashes of code and other structures form the Code Directory message that is signed. When used, algorithm_id is also set to the Code Signing enum value.
The Windows Application Package signing procedure that describes how file hashes are stored in the manifest, and how that manifest is signed.

serialization_id.description: The identifier of the normalized canonical serialization or signing-envelope scheme used to produce the deterministic byte sequence that was signed. A verifier must apply the same scheme to reproduce the signing input. Use Flat where the signed data is an opaque byte sequence, such as file content, to which no canonical serialization was applied. Distinct from algorithm_id, which identifies how the resulting bytes were signed; some signing formats (e.g. Authenticode) define their own canonicalization and populate both fields.

state.description: The digital signature state defines the signature state, normalized to the caption of 'state_id'. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

anyOf.description: The state is unknown.
The digital signature is valid.
The digital signature is invalid because its timestamp does not fall within the certificate's validity period.
The digital signature is invalid due to certificate revocation.
The digital signature is invalid due to certificate suspension.
The digital signature state is pending.
The digital signature is invalid because the certificate is rooted in an untrusted CA or is an untrusted self-signed certificate.
The digital signature is invalid because the certificate is explicitly distrusted. Note that whereas revocation is global, distrust reflects local IT/security policy.
The digital signature is invalid because the certificate is not intended for code signing purposes.
The digital signature is cryptographically invalid, e.g. a mismatched digest. This indicates possible tampering.
The digital signature is malformed and could not be processed.
The state is not mapped. See the state attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

state_id.description: The normalized identifier of the signature state.

OcsfDigitalSignature.title: OcsfDigitalSignature

OcsfDiscoveryDetails.description: The Discovery Details object describes results of a discovery task/job. Each result may be due to the violation of a rule associated with a policy and have multiple occurrences.

count.description: The number of discovered entities of the specified type.

occurrence_details.description: Details about where in the target entity, specified information was discovered. Only the attributes, relevant to the target entity type should be populated.

occurrences.description: Details about where in the target entity, specified information was discovered. Only the attributes, relevant to the target entity type should be populated.

rule.description: The rule associated with this discovery, usually part of the higher level policy from an enclosing class or object.

type.description: The specific type of information that was discovered. e.g. name, phone_number, etc.

value.description: Optionally, the specific value of discovered information.

OcsfDiscoveryDetails.title: OcsfDiscoveryDetails

OcsfDiscoveryEvent.description: The Discovery event is a generic event that defines a set of attributes available in Discovery category events. As a generic event, it could be used to log events that are not otherwise defined by the Discovery specific event classes.

anyOf.description: The action was unknown. The disposition_id attribute may still be set to a non-unknown value, for example 'Custom Action', 'Challenge'.
The activity was allowed. The disposition_id attribute should be set to a value that conforms to this action, for example 'Allowed', 'Approved', 'Delayed', 'No Action', 'Count' etc.

The attempted activity was denied. The disposition_id attribute should be set to a value that conforms to this action, for example 'Blocked', 'Rejected', 'Quarantined', 'Isolated', 'Dropped', 'Access Revoked, etc.

The activity was observed, but neither explicitly allowed nor denied. This is common with IDS and EDR controls that report additional information on observed behavior such as TTPs. The disposition_id attribute should be set to a value that conforms to this action, for example 'Logged', 'Alert', 'Detected', 'Count', etc.
The activity was modified, adjusted, or corrected. The disposition_id attribute should be set appropriately, for example 'Restored', 'Corrected', 'Delayed', 'Captcha', 'Tagged'.
The action is not mapped. See the action attribute which contains a data source specific value.

action_id.description: The action taken by a control or other policy-based system leading to an outcome or disposition. An unknown action may still correspond to a known disposition. Refer to disposition_id for the outcome of the action.

anyOf.description: The event activity is unknown.
The event activity is not mapped. See the activity_name attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

activity_id.description: The normalized identifier of the activity that triggered the event. Each event class defines its own set of activity values. Use 0 (Unknown) when the activity cannot be determined. Use 99 (Other) when the activity does not match any defined value, in which case activity_name must be populated with the source-specific label.

activity_name.description: The event activity name, as defined by the activity_id. When activity_id is 99 (Other), this attribute must contain the source-specific activity label. For all other activity_id values, this must match the caption defined for that activity_id enum value.

actor.description: The user, process, or service that initiated the activity on the host. For system-level events this is typically a process; for IAM events it is typically a user or role.

api.description: Describes details about a typical API (Application Programming Interface) call.

attacks.description: An array of MITRE ATT&CK® objects describing identified tactics, techniques & sub-techniques. The objects are compatible with MITRE ATLAS™ tactics, techniques & sub-techniques.

attestation_list.description: One or more cryptographic attestation objects over an event, each providing integrity, authenticity, and non-repudiation. Independent attesters over the same event — for example a producer at write time and a downstream processor at ingest — each contribute a separate attestation, distinct from co-signers on a single attestation, which share its signatures array. Carried on the record_integrity profile; the object itself is domain-agnostic.

authorizations.description: Provides details about an authorization, such as authorization outcome, and any associated policies related to the activity/event.

category_name.description: The event category name, as defined by the category_uid value. The value must match the caption defined for the corresponding category_uid enum value (e.g., "Findings" for category_uid: 2).

category_uid.description: The category unique identifier of the event. Each event class belongs to exactly one category. Producers and mappers must set this to the category defined by the event class being used.

class_name.description: The event class name, as defined by class_uid value: Base Event.

class_uid.description: The unique identifier of a class. A class describes the attributes available in an event. Producers and mappers must set this to the uid defined in the event class definition. For example, Detection Finding is 2004.

cloud.description: Describes details about the Cloud environment where the event or finding was created.

confidence.description: The confidence, normalized to the caption of the confidence_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

anyOf.description: The normalized confidence is unknown.
The confidence is not mapped to the defined enum values. See the confidence attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

confidence_id.description: The normalized confidence refers to the accuracy of the security control or alert. An analytic with a low confidence means that the alerts may be noisy or may not be malicious in nature.

confidence_score.description: The confidence score as reported by the event source. If confidence_id is 99 'Other', it should be the same as confidence if both are populated.

count.description: The number of events aggregated into this single record. Only populate for aggregate events. When set, start_time and end_time should also be provided to define the aggregation window.

device.description: The host or device where the activity was observed. Populate with details such as hostname, IP address, OS, and hardware identifiers when available from the source.

disposition.description: The disposition name, normalized to the caption of the disposition_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

anyOf.description: The disposition is unknown.
Granted access or allowed the action to the protected resource.
Denied access or blocked the action to the protected resource.
A suspicious file or other content was moved to a benign location.
A session was isolated on the network or within a browser.
A file or other content was deleted.
The request was detected as a threat and resulted in the connection being dropped.
A custom action was executed such as running of a command script. Use the message attribute of the base class for details.
A request or submission was approved. For example, when a form was properly filled out and submitted. This is distinct from 1 'Allowed'.
A quarantined file or other content was restored to its original location.
A suspicious or risky entity was deemed to no longer be suspicious (re-scored).
A corrupt file or configuration was corrected.
A corrupt file or configuration was partially corrected.
A corrupt file or configuration was not corrected.
An operation was delayed, for example if a restart was required to finish the operation.
Suspicious activity or a policy violation was detected without further action.
The outcome of an operation had no action taken.
The operation or action was logged without further action.
A file or other entity was marked with extended attributes.
The request or activity was detected as a threat and resulted in a notification but request was not blocked.
Counted the request or activity but did not determine whether to allow it or block it.
The request was detected as a threat and resulted in the connection being reset.
Required the end user to solve a CAPTCHA puzzle to prove that a human being is sending the request.
Ran a silent challenge that required the client session to verify that it's a browser, and not a bot.
The requestor's access has been revoked due to security policy enforcements. Note: use the Host profile if the User or Actor requestor is not present in the event class.
A request or submission was rejected. For example, when a form was improperly filled out and submitted. This is distinct from 2 'Blocked'.

An attempt to access a resource was denied due to an authorization check that failed. This is a more specific disposition than 2 'Blocked' and can be complemented with the authorizations attribute for more detail.
An error occurred during the processing of the activity or request. Use the message attribute of the base class for details.
The disposition is not mapped. See the disposition attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

Should be set to true if disposition_id = Alert among other dispositions, and/or risk_level_id or severity_id of the event is elevated. ja4_fingerprint_list.description: A list of the JA4+ network fingerprints.

load_balancer.description: The Load Balancer object contains information related to the device that is distributing incoming traffic to specified destinations.

malware.description: A list of Malware objects, describing details about the identified malware.

malware_scan_info.description: Describes details about the scan job that identified malware on the target system.

message.description: A human-readable description of the event, as defined by the source. This should be a concise, meaningful summary suitable for display in a UI or alert notification - not a raw log line. For example: "User john_doe logged in from 10.0.0.1." rather than a raw syslog string.

message_context.description: Communication context for AI system interactions including protocols, roles, clients, and session information for MCP and other AI communication systems.

metadata.description: The metadata object describes the event producer, schema version, and processing information. Producers and mappers must populate metadata.product to identify the data source, and metadata.version to indicate the OCSF schema version used. Consumers rely on this to interpret the event correctly.

network_observation_point.description: The network endpoint that observes or inspects network traffic as a third-party system, used when the observer is neither the source nor the destination of the communication (when observation_point_id = 3). Examples include network taps, span ports, inline security devices, or packet capture systems that monitor traffic between other endpoints.

observables.description: The observables array surfaces key indicators and entities from the event or finding in a single, consistent location for downstream correlation and detection. Each entry references an attribute path within the event (e.g., src_endpoint.ip) along with its type and value, enabling consumers to extract IOCs without parsing the full event structure.

observation_point.description: Indicates whether the source network endpoint, destination network endpoint, or neither served as the observation point for the activity. The value is normalized to the caption of the observation_point_id.

anyOf.description: The observation point is unknown.
The source network endpoint is the observation point.
The destination network endpoint is the observation point.
Neither the source nor destination network endpoint is the observation point. Refer to the network_observation_point attribute for details.

Both the source and destination network endpoint are the observation point. This typically occurs in localhost or internal communications where the source and destination are the same endpoint, often resulting in a connection_info.direction of Local.
The observation point is not mapped. See the observation_point attribute for a data source specific value.

observation_point_id.description: The normalized identifier of the observation point. The observation point identifier indicates whether the source network endpoint, destination network endpoint, or neither served as the observation point for the activity.

opcode.description: The DNS opcode specifies the type of the query message.

anyOf.description: Standard query
Inverse query, obsolete
Server status request
Reserved, not used
Zone change notification
Dynamic DNS update
DNS Stateful Operations (DSO)
The DNS Opcode is not defined by the RFC. See the opcode attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

opcode_id.description: The DNS opcode ID specifies the normalized query message type as defined in RFC 5395.

osint.description: The OSINT (Open Source Intelligence) object contains details related to an indicator such as the indicator itself, related indicators, geolocation, registrar information, subdomains, analyst commentary, and other contextual information. This information can be used to further enrich a detection or finding by providing decisioning support to other analysts and engineers.

packet_list.description: The list of packet objects describing captured network packets.

policy.description: The policy that pertains to the control that triggered the event, if applicable. For example the name of an anti-malware policy or an access control policy.

proxy.description: The proxy (server) in a network connection.

proxy_connection_info.description: The connection information from the proxy server to the remote server.

proxy_endpoint.description: The proxy (server) in a network connection.

proxy_http_request.description: The HTTP Request from the proxy server to the remote server.

proxy_http_response.description: The HTTP Response from the remote server to the proxy server.

proxy_tls.description: The TLS protocol negotiated between the proxy server and the remote server.

proxy_traffic.description: The network traffic refers to the amount of data moving across a network, from proxy to remote server at a given point of time.

query_additional.description: The Additional section of the DNS query message sent by the client, containing supplementary resource records and an optional TSIG record. A DNS message has at most one TSIG record; for a transaction with both query and response, the query TSIG is in query_additional.tsig and the response TSIG is in response_additional.tsig.

query_time.description: The Domain Name System (DNS) query time.

query_time_dt.description: The Domain Name System (DNS) query time.

raw_data.description: The original event/finding data as received from the source, before normalization into OCSF. Populate this with the verbatim log line, JSON payload, or other native format for forensic and debugging purposes. This field is not intended for structured querying - use the normalized OCSF attributes instead.

raw_data_hash.description: A fingerprint (hash) of the raw_data content. Use this to verify the integrity of the original event data or to deduplicate events.

raw_data_size.description: The size of the original event data (as captured in raw_data) in bytes, before OCSF normalization. Useful for metering and capacity planning.

rcode.description: The DNS server response code, normalized to the caption of the rcode_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

anyOf.description: No Error.
Format Error.
Server Failure.
Non-Existent Domain.
Not Implemented.
Query Refused.
Name Exists when it should not.
RR Set Exists when it should not.
RR Set that should exist does not.
Not Authorized or Server Not Authoritative for zone.
Name not contained in zone.
DSO-TYPE Not Implemented.
Bad EDNS OPT Version. Indicates that the client requested an EDNS version that the server does not support.
Key not recognized.
Signature out of time window.
Bad TKEY Mode.
Duplicate key name.
Algorithm not supported.
Bad Truncation.
Bad/missing Server Cookie.
The codes deemed to be unassigned by the RFC (unassigned codes: 12-15, 24-3840, 4096-65534).
The codes deemed to be reserved by the RFC (codes: 3841-4095, 65535).
The dns response code is not defined by the RFC.

rcode_id.description: The normalized identifier of the DNS server response code. See RFC 6895.

response_additional.description: The Additional section of the DNS response message sent by the server, containing supplementary resource records and an optional TSIG record. A DNS message has at most one TSIG record; for a transaction with both query and response, the query TSIG is in query_additional.tsig and the response TSIG is in response_additional.tsig.

response_time.description: The Domain Name System (DNS) response time.

response_time_dt.description: The Domain Name System (DNS) response time.

risk_details.description: Describes the risk associated with the finding.

risk_level.description: The risk level, normalized to the caption of the risk_level_id value.

anyOf.description: The risk level is not mapped. See the risk_level attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

risk_score.description: The risk score as reported by the event source.

severity.description: The event/finding severity label, normalized to the caption of the severity_id value. When severity_id is 99 (Other), this attribute must contain the source-specific severity label. For all other values, this should match the caption defined for that severity_id enum value (e.g., "High" for severity_id: 4).

anyOf.description: The event/finding severity is unknown.
Informational message. No action required.
The user decides if action is needed.
Action is required but the situation is not serious at this time.
Action is required immediately.
Action is required immediately and the scope is broad.
An error occurred but it is too late to take remedial action.
The event/finding severity is not mapped. See the severity attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

severity_id.description:
The normalized identifier of the event/finding severity.

The normalized severity is a measurement the effort and expense required to manage and resolve an event or incident. Smaller numerical values represent lower impact events, and larger numerical values represent higher impact events.

src_endpoint.description: The initiator (client) of the network connection.

start_time.description: The time of the earliest event in an aggregate (count > 1). Do not populate for discrete, point-in-time events - use time alone. Subclasses such as findings may redefine this for their own time-range semantics.

start_time_dt.description: The time of the earliest event in an aggregate (count > 1). Do not populate for discrete, point-in-time events - use time alone. Subclasses such as findings may redefine this for their own time-range semantics.

status.description: The event status label, normalized to the caption of the status_id value. When status_id is 99 (Other), this attribute must contain the source-specific status label. For all other values, this must match the caption defined for that status_id enum value (e.g., "Success" for status_id: 1).

status_code.description: The source-specific status or error code as reported by the event source. For example, a Windows logon failure code (0x18), an HTTP response code (403), or an AWS API error code. This preserves the original code for detailed troubleshooting beyond what status_id conveys.

status_detail.description: A human-readable description providing additional context about the event outcome. Use this to convey details that go beyond the normalized status_id and source-specific status_code, such as a failure reason or error message. For example: "Account locked after 5 failed attempts.".

anyOf.description: The status is unknown.
The activity completed successfully.
The activity failed.
The status is not mapped. See the status attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

status_id.description: The normalized status of the event outcome. Use this family of attributes to convey the outcome of the activity described by the event. Producers should map their source outcome to 1 (Success) or 2 (Failure). Use 0 (Unknown) when the outcome cannot be determined, and 99 (Other) with a populated status string when the source value does not map cleanly.

time.description: The primary timestamp of the event - when the activity actually occurred at the source. This does not capture when the event record was created or serialized by the source system; for event lifecycle timestamps such as ingestion and processing, use metadata.logged_time and metadata.processed_time respectively, or the equivalent attributes in the metadata.loggers array when recording pipeline stages. For aggregate events (count > 1), set this to start_time (the earliest OCSF time in the aggregate) to preserve causal ordering and consistent timeline alignment. Note: finding classes redefine time as the finding creation time rather than the activity occurrence time. This must be a UTC epoch value in milliseconds (e.g., 1776881335332). Mappers should use the most precise and authoritative timestamp available from the source.

time_dt.description: The primary timestamp of the event - when the activity actually occurred at the source. This does not capture when the event record was created or serialized by the source system; for event lifecycle timestamps such as ingestion and processing, use metadata.logged_time and metadata.processed_time respectively, or the equivalent attributes in the metadata.loggers array when recording pipeline stages. For aggregate events (count > 1), set this to start_time (the earliest OCSF time in the aggregate) to preserve causal ordering and consistent timeline alignment. Note: finding classes redefine time as the finding creation time rather than the activity occurrence time. This must be a UTC epoch value in milliseconds (e.g., 1776881335332). Mappers should use the most precise and authoritative timestamp available from the source.

timezone_offset.description: The number of minutes that the reported event time is ahead or behind UTC, in the range -1,080 to +1,080. This allows consumers to reconstruct the local time at the event source. For example, US Eastern Standard Time is -300. Populate this when the source provides local time zone information.

traffic.description: The network traffic for this observation period. Use when reporting: (1) delta values (bytes/packets transferred since the last observation), (2) instantaneous measurements at a specific point in time, or (3) standalone single-event metrics. This attribute represents a point-in-time measurement or incremental change, not a running total. For accumulated totals across multiple observations or the lifetime of a flow, use cumulative_traffic instead.

transaction_id.description: The 16-bit DNS transaction identifier assigned by the client and echoed unchanged in the server response. This value is the same for both the query and response messages.

type_name.description: The event/finding type name, combining the class and activity (e.g., "Detection Finding: Create"). The value must match the class_name and activity_name joined by ": ".

anyOf.description: The DNS query request.
The DNS query response.
Bidirectional DNS request and response traffic.

type_uid.description: The event/finding type ID. It identifies the event's semantics and structure. Producers and mappers must compute this as class_uid * 100 + activity_id. It uniquely identifies the combination of event class and activity across the entire schema. For example, Detection Finding: Create is 200401.

unmapped.description:
A container for source-specific attributes that do not map to any defined OCSF attribute. Use this to preserve valuable source data that would otherwise be lost during normalization. The keys and values are specific to the event source.

Note: Consumers should not rely on a stable structure within this field. The preferred approach to unmapped attributes is to create a custom extension with the desired structure.

OcsfDnsActivity.title: OcsfDnsActivity

OcsfDnsAnswer.description: The DNS Answer object represents a specific response provided by the Domain Name System (DNS) when querying for information about a domain or performing a DNS operation. It encapsulates the relevant details and data returned by the DNS server in response to a query.

class.description: The class of DNS data contained in this resource record. See RFC 1035. For example: IN.

flag_ids.description: The list of DNS answer header flag IDs.

anyOf.description: The flag is unknown.
The flag is not mapped. See the flags attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

flags.description: The list of DNS answer header flags.

hostname.description: The owner name of the resource record. For example: www.example.com.

packet_uid.description: The DNS packet identifier assigned by the program that generated the query. The identifier is copied to the response.

rdata.description: The data describing the DNS resource. The meaning of this data depends on the type and class of the resource record.

ttl.description: The time interval that the resource record may be cached. Zero value means that the resource record can only be used for the transaction in progress, and should not be cached.

type.description: The type of data contained in this resource record. See RFC 1035. For example: CNAME.

OcsfDnsAnswer.title: OcsfDnsAnswer

OcsfDnsQuery.description: The DNS Query object represents a specific request made to the Domain Name System (DNS) to retrieve information about a domain or perform a DNS operation.

class.description: The class of resource records being queried. See RFC 1035. For example: IN.

hostname.description: The hostname or domain being queried. For example: www.example.com

opcode.description: The DNS opcode specifies the type of the query message.

anyOf.description: Standard query
Inverse query, obsolete
Server status request
Reserved, not used
Zone change notification
Dynamic DNS update
DNS Stateful Operations (DSO)
The DNS Opcode is not defined by the RFC. See the opcode attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

opcode_id.description: The DNS opcode ID specifies the normalized query message type as defined in RFC 5395.

packet_uid.description: The DNS packet identifier assigned by the program that generated the query. The identifier is copied to the response.

type.description: The type of resource records being queried. See RFC 1035. For example: A, AAAA, CNAME, MX, and NS.

OcsfDnsQuery.title: OcsfDnsQuery

OcsfDnsResourceRecord.description: The DNS Resource Record object represents a single resource record as defined in RFC 1035. It is used in the Answer, Authority, and Additional sections of a DNS message.

class.description: The class of DNS data contained in this resource record. See RFC 1035. For example: IN.

hostname.description: The owner name of the resource record. For example: www.example.com.

rdata.description: The data describing the DNS resource. The meaning of this data depends on the type and class of the resource record.

ttl.description: The time interval that the resource record may be cached. Zero value means that the resource record can only be used for the transaction in progress, and should not be cached.

type.description: The type of data contained in this resource record. See RFC 1035. For example: CNAME.

OcsfDnsResourceRecord.title: OcsfDnsResourceRecord

OcsfDnsSection.description: The DNS Section object represents a DNS message section that carries supplementary resource records alongside an optional TSIG record. It is used for both the client Additional section (query_additional) and the server Additional section (response_additional) of a DNS message. A DNS message has at most one TSIG record, which authenticates the entire message.

records.description: The resource records contained in this DNS section.

tsig.description: The TSIG (Transaction Signature) record present in this DNS section, used to authenticate the entire DNS message. Per RFC 2845, at most one TSIG record is permitted per DNS message.

OcsfDnsSection.title: OcsfDnsSection

OcsfDomainContact.description: The contact information related to a domain registration, e.g., registrant, administrator, abuse, billing, or technical contact.

location.description: Location details for the contract such as the city, state/province, country, etc.

name.description: The individual or organization name for the contact.

phone_number.description: The number associated with the phone.

type.description: The Domain Contact type, normalized to the caption of the type_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the source

anyOf.description: The type is unknown.
The contact information provided is for the domain registrant.
The contact information provided is for the domain administrator.
The contact information provided is for the domain technical lead.
The contact information provided is for the domain billing lead.
The contact information provided is for the domain abuse contact.
The type is not mapped. See the type attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

type_id.description: The normalized domain contact type ID.

uid.description: The unique identifier of the contact information, typically provided in WHOIS information.

OcsfDomainContact.title: OcsfDomainContact

OcsfDownloadInfo.description: The Download Info object contains metadata pertaining to a downloaded file.

referrer.description: The URL that referred to src_url. This is typically the URL of a web page containing a download link.

src_endpoint.description: Information about the network endpoint from which the file was downloaded.

src_url.description: The URL from which the file was downloaded.

type.description: The download type, normalized to the caption of the type_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

anyOf.description: The file's download type is unknown.
The file was downloaded from a server running on device.
The file was downloaded from an intranet server.
The file was downloaded from a trusted server.
The file was downloaded from an internet server.
The file was downloaded from an untrusted server.
The file's download type is not mapped. See the type attribute, which contains an event source specific value.

type_id.description: The download type ID. The values correspond to the five permitted values of the ZoneId property in the Mark of the Web metadata of a downloaded file on Windows. Note however that each numeric value is 1 greater than its ZoneId equivalent.

OcsfDownloadInfo.title: OcsfDownloadInfo

OcsfDroneFlightsActivity.description: Drone Flights Activity events report the activity of Unmanned Aerial Systems (UAS), their Operators, and mission-planning and authorization metadata as reported by the UAS platforms themselves, by Counter-UAS (CUAS) systems, or other remote monitoring or sensing infrastructure. Based on the Remote ID defined in Standard Specification for Remote ID and Tracking (ASTM Designation: F3411-22a).

anyOf.description: The action was unknown. The disposition_id attribute may still be set to a non-unknown value, for example 'Custom Action', 'Challenge'.
The activity was allowed. The disposition_id attribute should be set to a value that conforms to this action, for example 'Allowed', 'Approved', 'Delayed', 'No Action', 'Count' etc.

The attempted activity was denied. The disposition_id attribute should be set to a value that conforms to this action, for example 'Blocked', 'Rejected', 'Quarantined', 'Isolated', 'Dropped', 'Access Revoked, etc.

The activity was observed, but neither explicitly allowed nor denied. This is common with IDS and EDR controls that report additional information on observed behavior such as TTPs. The disposition_id attribute should be set to a value that conforms to this action, for example 'Logged', 'Alert', 'Detected', 'Count', etc.
The activity was modified, adjusted, or corrected. The disposition_id attribute should be set appropriately, for example 'Restored', 'Corrected', 'Delayed', 'Captcha', 'Tagged'.
The action is not mapped. See the action attribute which contains a data source specific value.

action_id.description: The action taken by a control or other policy-based system leading to an outcome or disposition. An unknown action may still correspond to a known disposition. Refer to disposition_id for the outcome of the action.

anyOf.description: The event activity is unknown.
Remote ID information from an Unmanned System is being captured (collected).
Unmanned System activity is being recorded.
The event activity is not mapped. See the activity_name attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

activity_id.description: The normalized identifier of the activity that triggered the event. Each event class defines its own set of activity values. Use 0 (Unknown) when the activity cannot be determined. Use 99 (Other) when the activity does not match any defined value, in which case activity_name must be populated with the source-specific label.

activity_name.description: The event activity name, as defined by the activity_id. When activity_id is 99 (Other), this attribute must contain the source-specific activity label. For all other activity_id values, this must match the caption defined for that activity_id enum value.

actor.description: The user, process, or service that initiated the activity on the host. For system-level events this is typically a process; for IAM events it is typically a user or role.

api.description: Describes details about a typical API (Application Programming Interface) call.

attacks.description: An array of MITRE ATT&CK® objects describing identified tactics, techniques & sub-techniques. The objects are compatible with MITRE ATLAS™ tactics, techniques & sub-techniques.

attestation_list.description: One or more cryptographic attestation objects over an event, each providing integrity, authenticity, and non-repudiation. Independent attesters over the same event — for example a producer at write time and a downstream processor at ingest — each contribute a separate attestation, distinct from co-signers on a single attestation, which share its signatures array. Carried on the record_integrity profile; the object itself is domain-agnostic.

auth_protocol.description: The authentication type as defined by the caption of auth_protocol_id. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

anyOf.description: The authentication type is unknown.
The authentication type is not mapped. See the auth_protocol attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

auth_protocol_id.description: The normalized identifier of the authentication type used to authorize a flight plan or mission.

authorizations.description: Provides details about an authorization, such as authorization outcome, and any associated policies related to the activity/event.

category_name.description: The event category name, as defined by category_uid value: Unmanned Systems.

category_uid.description: The category unique identifier of the event. Each event class belongs to exactly one category. Producers and mappers must set this to the category defined by the event class being used.

class_name.description: The event class name, as defined by class_uid value: Drone Flights Activity.

class_uid.description: The unique identifier of a class. A class describes the attributes available in an event. Producers and mappers must set this to the uid defined in the event class definition. For example, Detection Finding is 2004.

classification.description: UA Classification - Allows a region to classify UAS in a regional specific manner. The format may differ from region to region.

cloud.description: Describes details about the Cloud environment where the event or finding was created.

comment.description: This optional, free-text field enables the operator to describe the purpose of a flight, if so desired.

confidence.description: The confidence, normalized to the caption of the confidence_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

anyOf.description: The normalized confidence is unknown.
The confidence is not mapped to the defined enum values. See the confidence attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

confidence_id.description: The normalized confidence refers to the accuracy of the security control or alert. An analytic with a low confidence means that the alerts may be noisy or may not be malicious in nature.

confidence_score.description: The confidence score as reported by the event source. If confidence_id is 99 'Other', it should be the same as confidence if both are populated.

count.description: The number of events aggregated into this single record. Only populate for aggregate events. When set, start_time and end_time should also be provided to define the aggregation window.

device.description: The host or device where the activity was observed. Populate with details such as hostname, IP address, OS, and hardware identifiers when available from the source.

disposition.description: The disposition name, normalized to the caption of the disposition_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

anyOf.description: The disposition is unknown.
Granted access or allowed the action to the protected resource.
Denied access or blocked the action to the protected resource.
A suspicious file or other content was moved to a benign location.
A session was isolated on the network or within a browser.
A file or other content was deleted.
The request was detected as a threat and resulted in the connection being dropped.
A custom action was executed such as running of a command script. Use the message attribute of the base class for details.
A request or submission was approved. For example, when a form was properly filled out and submitted. This is distinct from 1 'Allowed'.
A quarantined file or other content was restored to its original location.
A suspicious or risky entity was deemed to no longer be suspicious (re-scored).
A corrupt file or configuration was corrected.
A corrupt file or configuration was partially corrected.
A corrupt file or configuration was not corrected.
An operation was delayed, for example if a restart was required to finish the operation.
Suspicious activity or a policy violation was detected without further action.
The outcome of an operation had no action taken.
The operation or action was logged without further action.
A file or other entity was marked with extended attributes.
The request or activity was detected as a threat and resulted in a notification but request was not blocked.
Counted the request or activity but did not determine whether to allow it or block it.
The request was detected as a threat and resulted in the connection being reset.
Required the end user to solve a CAPTCHA puzzle to prove that a human being is sending the request.
Ran a silent challenge that required the client session to verify that it's a browser, and not a bot.
The requestor's access has been revoked due to security policy enforcements. Note: use the Host profile if the User or Actor requestor is not present in the event class.
A request or submission was rejected. For example, when a form was improperly filled out and submitted. This is distinct from 2 'Blocked'.

An attempt to access a resource was denied due to an authorization check that failed. This is a more specific disposition than 2 'Blocked' and can be complemented with the authorizations attribute for more detail.
An error occurred during the processing of the activity or request. Use the message attribute of the base class for details.
The disposition is not mapped. See the disposition attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

disposition_id.description: Describes the outcome or action taken by a security control, such as access control checks, malware detections or various types of policy violations.

dst_endpoint.description: The destination network endpoint of the Unmanned Aerial System (UAS), Counter Unmanned Aerial System (CUAS) platform, or other unmanned systems monitoring and/or sensing infrastructure.

duration.description: The elapsed time of the aggregation window in milliseconds, from start_time to end_time. Only populate for aggregate events (count > 1). The value should equal end_time - start_time.

end_time.description: The time of the most recent event in an aggregate (count > 1). Do not populate for discrete, point-in-time events - use time alone. Subclasses such as findings may redefine this for their own time-range semantics.

end_time_dt.description: The time of the most recent event in an aggregate (count > 1). Do not populate for discrete, point-in-time events - use time alone. Subclasses such as findings may redefine this for their own time-range semantics.

enrichments.description:
The additional information from an external data source, which is associated with the event or a finding. For example add location information for the IP address in the DNS answers:

[{"name": "answers.ip", "value": "92.24.47.250", "type": "location", "data": {"city": "Socotra", "continent": "Asia", "coordinates": [-25.4153, 17.0743], "country": "YE", "desc": "Yemen"}}]

firewall_rule.description: The firewall rule that pertains to the control that triggered the event, if applicable.

is_alert.description: Indicates that the event is considered to be an alertable signal. Should be set to true if disposition_id = Alert among other dispositions, and/or risk_level_id or severity_id of the event is elevated. Not all control events will be alertable, for example if disposition_id = Exonerated or disposition_id = Allowed.

malware.description: A list of Malware objects, describing details about the identified malware.

malware_scan_info.description: Describes details about the scan job that identified malware on the target system.

message.description: A human-readable description of the event, as defined by the source. This should be a concise, meaningful summary suitable for display in a UI or alert notification - not a raw log line. For example: "User john_doe logged in from 10.0.0.1." rather than a raw syslog string.

metadata.description: The metadata object describes the event producer, schema version, and processing information. Producers and mappers must populate metadata.product to identify the data source, and metadata.version to indicate the OCSF schema version used. Consumers rely on this to interpret the event correctly.

observables.description: The observables array surfaces key indicators and entities from the event or finding in a single, consistent location for downstream correlation and detection. Each entry references an attribute path within the event (e.g., src_endpoint.ip) along with its type and value, enabling consumers to extract IOCs without parsing the full event structure.

osint.description: The OSINT (Open Source Intelligence) object contains details related to an indicator such as the indicator itself, related indicators, geolocation, registrar information, subdomains, analyst commentary, and other contextual information. This information can be used to further enrich a detection or finding by providing decisioning support to other analysts and engineers.

policy.description: The policy that pertains to the control that triggered the event, if applicable. For example the name of an anti-malware policy or an access control policy.

protocol_name.description: The networking protocol associated with the Remote ID device or beacon. E.g. BLE, LTE, 802.11.

proxy_endpoint.description: The proxy (server) in a network connection.

raw_data.description: The original event/finding data as received from the source, before normalization into OCSF. Populate this with the verbatim log line, JSON payload, or other native format for forensic and debugging purposes. This field is not intended for structured querying - use the normalized OCSF attributes instead.

raw_data_hash.description: A fingerprint (hash) of the raw_data content. Use this to verify the integrity of the original event data or to deduplicate events.

raw_data_size.description: The size of the original event data (as captured in raw_data) in bytes, before OCSF normalization. Useful for metering and capacity planning.

risk_details.description: Describes the risk associated with the finding.

risk_level.description: The risk level, normalized to the caption of the risk_level_id value.

anyOf.description: The risk level is not mapped. See the risk_level attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

risk_score.description: The risk score as reported by the event source.

severity.description: The event/finding severity label, normalized to the caption of the severity_id value. When severity_id is 99 (Other), this attribute must contain the source-specific severity label. For all other values, this should match the caption defined for that severity_id enum value (e.g., "High" for severity_id: 4).

anyOf.description: The event/finding severity is unknown.
Informational message. No action required.
The user decides if action is needed.
Action is required but the situation is not serious at this time.
Action is required immediately.
Action is required immediately and the scope is broad.
An error occurred but it is too late to take remedial action.
The event/finding severity is not mapped. See the severity attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

severity_id.description:
The normalized identifier of the event/finding severity.

The normalized severity is a measurement the effort and expense required to manage and resolve an event or incident. Smaller numerical values represent lower impact events, and larger numerical values represent higher impact events.

src_endpoint.description: The source network endpoint of the Unmanned Aerial System (UAS), Counter Unmanned Aerial System (CUAS) platform, or other unmanned systems monitoring and/or sensing infrastructure.

start_time.description: The time of the earliest event in an aggregate (count > 1). Do not populate for discrete, point-in-time events - use time alone. Subclasses such as findings may redefine this for their own time-range semantics.

start_time_dt.description: The time of the earliest event in an aggregate (count > 1). Do not populate for discrete, point-in-time events - use time alone. Subclasses such as findings may redefine this for their own time-range semantics.

status.description: The normalized Operational status for the Unmanned Aerial System (UAS) normalized to the caption of the status_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the source.

status_code.description: The source-specific status or error code as reported by the event source. For example, a Windows logon failure code (0x18), an HTTP response code (403), or an AWS API error code. This preserves the original code for detailed troubleshooting beyond what status_id conveys.

status_detail.description: A human-readable description providing additional context about the event outcome. Use this to convey details that go beyond the normalized status_id and source-specific status_code, such as a failure reason or error message. For example: "Account locked after 5 failed attempts.".

anyOf.description: The status is unknown.
The operational status is not reported.
The Unmanned Aerial System (UAS) is grounded.
The Unmanned Aerial System (UAS) is airborne.
The Unmanned Aerial System (UAS) is reporting an emergency status.
The Unmanned Aerial System (UAS) is reporting the Remote ID beacon or device is malfunctioning or has failed.
An ASTM Reserved status is reported.
The status is not mapped. See the status attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

status_id.description: The normalized Operational status identifier for the Unmanned Aerial System (UAS).

time.description: The primary timestamp of the event - when the activity actually occurred at the source. This does not capture when the event record was created or serialized by the source system; for event lifecycle timestamps such as ingestion and processing, use metadata.logged_time and metadata.processed_time respectively, or the equivalent attributes in the metadata.loggers array when recording pipeline stages. For aggregate events (count > 1), set this to start_time (the earliest OCSF time in the aggregate) to preserve causal ordering and consistent timeline alignment. Note: finding classes redefine time as the finding creation time rather than the activity occurrence time. This must be a UTC epoch value in milliseconds (e.g., 1776881335332). Mappers should use the most precise and authoritative timestamp available from the source.

time_dt.description: The primary timestamp of the event - when the activity actually occurred at the source. This does not capture when the event record was created or serialized by the source system; for event lifecycle timestamps such as ingestion and processing, use metadata.logged_time and metadata.processed_time respectively, or the equivalent attributes in the metadata.loggers array when recording pipeline stages. For aggregate events (count > 1), set this to start_time (the earliest OCSF time in the aggregate) to preserve causal ordering and consistent timeline alignment. Note: finding classes redefine time as the finding creation time rather than the activity occurrence time. This must be a UTC epoch value in milliseconds (e.g., 1776881335332). Mappers should use the most precise and authoritative timestamp available from the source.

timezone_offset.description: The number of minutes that the reported event time is ahead or behind UTC, in the range -1,080 to +1,080. This allows consumers to reconstruct the local time at the event source. For example, US Eastern Standard Time is -300. Populate this when the source provides local time zone information.

traffic.description: Traffic refers to the amount of data transmitted from a Unmanned Aerial System (UAS) or Counter Unmanned Aerial System (UAS) (CUAS) system at a given point of time. Ex: bytes_in and bytes_out.

type_name.description: The event/finding type name, combining the class and activity (e.g., "Detection Finding: Create"). The value must match the class_name and activity_name joined by ": ".

anyOf.description: Remote ID information from an Unmanned System is being captured (collected).
Unmanned System activity is being recorded.
The event activity is not mapped. See the activity_name attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

type_uid.description: The event/finding type ID. It identifies the event's semantics and structure. Producers and mappers must compute this as class_uid * 100 + activity_id. It uniquely identifies the combination of event class and activity across the entire schema. For example, Detection Finding: Create is 200401.

unmanned_aerial_system.description: The Unmanned Aerial System object describes the characteristics, Position Location Information (PLI), and other metadata of Unmanned Aerial Systems (UAS) and other unmanned and drone systems used in Remote ID. Remote ID is defined in the Standard Specification for Remote ID and Tracking (ASTM Designation: F3411-22a).

unmanned_system_operating_area.description: The UAS Operating Area object describes details about a precise area of operations for a UAS flight or mission.

unmanned_system_operator.description: The human or machine operator of an Unmanned System.

unmapped.description:
A container for source-specific attributes that do not map to any defined OCSF attribute. Use this to preserve valuable source data that would otherwise be lost during normalization. The keys and values are specific to the event source.

Note: Consumers should not rely on a stable structure within this field. The preferred approach to unmapped attributes is to create a custom extension with the desired structure.

OcsfEdge.description: Represents a connection or relationship between two nodes in a graph.

data.description: Additional data about the edge such as weight, distance, or custom properties.

is_directed.description: Indicates whether the edge is (true) or undirected (false).

name.description: The human-readable name or label for the edge.

relation.description: The type of relationship between nodes (e.g. is-attached-to , depends-on, etc).

source.description: The unique identifier of the node where the edge originates.

target.description: The unique identifier of the node where the edge terminates.

uid.description: Unique identifier of the edge.

uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

OcsfEmail.description: The Email object describes the email metadata such as sender, recipients, and direction, and can include embedded URLs and files.

bcc.description: The machine-readable email header Bcc values, as defined by RFC 5322. For example example.user@usersdomain.com.

bcc_mailboxes.description: The human-readable email header Bcc Mailbox values. For example 'Example User <example.user@usersdomain.com>'.

cc.description: The machine-readable email header Cc values, as defined by RFC 5322. For example example.user@usersdomain.com.

cc_mailboxes.description: The human-readable email header Cc Mailbox values. For example 'Example User <example.user@usersdomain.com>'.

data_classification.description: The Data Classification object includes information about data classification levels and data category types.

data_classifications.description: A list of Data Classification objects, that include information about data classification levels and data category types, identified by a classifier.

delivered_to.description: The machine-readable Delivered-To email header field. For example example.user@usersdomain.com

delivered_to_list.description: The machine-readable Delivered-To email header values. For example example.user@usersdomain.com

files.description: The files embedded or attached to the email.

from.description: The machine-readable email header From value, as defined by RFC 5322. For example example.user@usersdomain.com.

from_list.description: The machine-readable email header From values. This array should contain the value in from. For example example.user@usersdomain.com.

from_mailbox.description: The human-readable email header From Mailbox value. For example 'Example User <example.user@usersdomain.com>'.

from_mailboxes.description: The human-readable email header From Mailbox values. This array should contain the value in from_mailbox. For example 'Example User <example.user@usersdomain.com>'.

http_headers.description: Additional HTTP headers of an HTTP request or response.

is_read.description: The indication of whether the email has been read.

message_uid.description: The email header Message-ID value, as defined by RFC 5322.

reply_to.description: The machine-readable email header Reply-To value, as defined by RFC 5322. For example example.user@usersdomain.com

reply_to_list.description: The machine-readable email header Reply-To values, as defined by RFC 5322. For example example.user@usersdomain.com

reply_to_mailboxes.description: The human-readable email header Reply To Mailbox values. For example 'Example User <example.user@usersdomain.com>'.

return_path.description: The address found in the 'Return-Path' header, which indicates where bounce messages (non-delivery reports) should be sent. This address is often set by the sending system and may differ from the 'From' or 'Sender' addresses. For example, mailer-daemon@senderserver.com.

sender.description: The machine readable email address of the system or server that actually transmitted the email message, extracted from the email headers per RFC 5322. This differs from the from field, which shows the message author. The sender field is most commonly used when multiple addresses appear in the from_list field, or when the transmitting system is different from the message author (such as when sending on behalf of someone else).

sender_mailbox.description: The human readable email address of the system or server that actually transmitted the email message, extracted from the email headers per RFC 5322. This differs from the from_mailbox field, which shows the message author. The sender mailbox field is most commonly used when multiple addresses appear in the from_mailboxes field, or when the transmitting system is different from the message author (such as when sending on behalf of someone else).

size.description: The size in bytes of the email, including attachments.

smtp_from.description: The value of the SMTP MAIL FROM command.

smtp_to.description: The value of the SMTP envelope RCPT TO command.

subject.description: The email header Subject value, as defined by RFC 5322.

to.description: The machine-readable email header To values, as defined by RFC 5322. For example example.user@usersdomain.com

to_mailboxes.description: The human-readable email header To Mailbox values. For example 'Example User <example.user@usersdomain.com>'.

uid.description: The unique identifier of the email thread.

urls.description: The URLs embedded in the email.

x_originating_ip.description: The X-Originating-IP header identifying the emails originating IP address(es).
