OcsfKeyValueObject.description: A generic object allowing to define a {key:value} pair.

name.description: The name of the key.

value.description: The value associated to the key.

values.description: Optional, the values associated to the key. You can populate this attribute, when you have multiple values for the same key.

OcsfKeyValueObject.title: OcsfKeyValueObject

OcsfKeyboardInfo.description: The Keyboard Information object contains details and attributes related to a computer or device keyboard. It encompasses information that describes the characteristics, capabilities, and configuration of the keyboard.

function_keys.description: The number of function keys on client keyboard.

ime.description: The Input Method Editor (IME) file name.

keyboard_layout.description: The keyboard locale identifier name (e.g., en-US).

OcsfKeyboardInfo.title: OcsfKeyboardInfo

OcsfKillChainPhase.description: The Kill Chain Phase object represents a single phase of a cyber attack, including the initial reconnaissance and planning stages up to the final objective of the attacker. It provides a detailed description of each phase and its associated activities within the broader context of a cyber attack.

anyOf.description: The kill chain phase is unknown.

The attackers pick a target and perform a detailed analysis, start collecting information (email addresses, conferences information, etc.) and evaluate the victim’s vulnerabilities to determine how to exploit them.
The attackers develop a malware weapon and aim to exploit the discovered vulnerabilities.
The intruders will use various tactics, such as phishing, infected USB drives, etc.
The intruders start leveraging vulnerabilities to executed code on the victim’s system.
The intruders install malware on the victim’s system.
Malware opens a command channel to enable the intruders to remotely manipulate the victim's system.
With hands-on keyboard access, intruders accomplish the mission’s goal.
The kill chain phase is not mapped. See the phase attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

phase_id.description: The cyber kill chain phase identifier.

OcsfKillChainPhase.title: OcsfKillChainPhase

OcsfLdapPerson.description: The additional LDAP attributes that describe a person.

cost_center.description: The cost center associated with the user.

created_time.description: The timestamp when the user was created.

created_time_dt.description: The timestamp when the user was created.

deleted_time.description: The timestamp when the user was deleted. In Active Directory (AD), when a user is deleted they are moved to a temporary container and then removed after 30 days. So, this field can be populated even after a user is deleted for the next 30 days.

deleted_time_dt.description: The timestamp when the user was deleted. In Active Directory (AD), when a user is deleted they are moved to a temporary container and then removed after 30 days. So, this field can be populated even after a user is deleted for the next 30 days.

department.description: The name of the department in which the user works.

display_name.description: The display name of the LDAP person. According to RFC 2798, this is the preferred name of a person to be used when displaying entries.

email_addrs.description: A list of additional email addresses for the user.

employee_uid.description: The employee identifier assigned to the user by the organization.

given_name.description: The given or first name of the user.

hire_time.description: The timestamp when the user was or will be hired by the organization.

hire_time_dt.description: The timestamp when the user was or will be hired by the organization.

labels.description: The labels associated with the user. For example in AD this could be the userType, employeeType. For example: Member, Employee.

last_login_time.description: The last time when the user logged in.

last_login_time_dt.description: The last time when the user logged in.

ldap_cn.description: The LDAP and X.500 commonName attribute, typically the full name of the person. For example, John Doe.

ldap_dn.description: The X.500 Distinguished Name (DN) is a structured string that uniquely identifies an entry, such as a user, in an X.500 directory service For example, cn=John Doe,ou=People,dc=example,dc=com.

leave_time.description: The timestamp when the user left or will be leaving the organization.

leave_time_dt.description: The timestamp when the user left or will be leaving the organization.

location.description: The geographical location associated with a user. This is typically the user's usual work location.

manager.description: The user's manager. This helps in understanding an org hierarchy. This should only ever be populated once in an event. I.e. there should not be a manager's manager in an event.

modified_time.description: The timestamp when the user entry was last modified.

modified_time_dt.description: The timestamp when the user entry was last modified.

office_location.description: The primary office location associated with the user. This could be any string and isn't a specific address. For example, South East Virtual.

phone_number.description: The telephone number of the user. Corresponds to the LDAP Telephone-Number CN.

surname.description: The last or family name for the user.

tags.description: The list of tags; {key:value} pairs associated to the user.

OcsfLdapPerson.title: OcsfLdapPerson

OcsfLinuxUsersProfile.description: The attributes that Linux uses to identify user information.

auid.description: The audit user assigned at login by the audit subsystem.

egid.description: The effective group under which this process is running.

euid.description: The effective user under which this process is running.

group.description: The group under which this process is running.

OcsfLinuxUsersProfile.title: OcsfLinuxUsersProfile

OcsfLoadBalancer.description: The load balancer object describes the load balancer entity and contains additional information regarding the distribution of traffic across a network.

classification.description: The request classification as defined by the load balancer.

code.description: The numeric response status code detailing the connection from the load balancer to the destination target.

dst_endpoint.description: The destination to which the load balancer is distributing traffic.

endpoint_connections.description: An object detailing the load balancer connection attempts and responses.

ip.description: The IP address of the load balancer node that handled the client request. Note: the load balancer may have other IP addresses, and this is not an IP address of the target/distribution endpoint - see dst_endpoint.

message.description: The load balancer message.

metrics.description: General purpose metrics associated with the load balancer.

name.description: The name of the load balancer.

status_detail.description: The status detail contains additional status information about the load balancer distribution event.

uid.description: The unique identifier for the load balancer.

uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

OcsfLoadBalancer.title: OcsfLoadBalancer

OcsfLoadBalancerProfile.description: The attributes that describe information specific to load balancers.

load_balancer.description: The Load Balancer object contains information related to the device that is distributing incoming traffic to specified destinations.

OcsfLoadBalancerProfile.title: OcsfLoadBalancerProfile

OcsfLocation.description: The Geo Location object describes a geographical location, usually associated with an IP address.

aerial_height.description: Expressed as either height above takeoff location or height above ground level (AGL) for a UAS current location. This value is provided in meters and must have a minimum resolution of 1 m. Special Values: Invalid, No Value, or Unknown: -1000 m.

coordinates.description: A two-element array, containing a longitude/latitude pair. The format conforms with GeoJSON. For example: [-73.983, 40.719].

country.description:
The ISO 3166-1 Alpha-2 country code.

Note: The two letter country code should be capitalized. For example: US or CA.

desc.description: The description of the geographical location.

geodetic_altitude.description: The aircraft distance above or below the ellipsoid as measured along a line that passes through the aircraft and is normal to the surface of the WGS-84 ellipsoid. This value is provided in meters and must have a minimum resolution of 1 m. Special Values: Invalid, No Value, or Unknown: -1000 m.

geodetic_vertical_accuracy.description: Provides quality/containment on geodetic altitude. This is based on ADS-B Geodetic Vertical Accuracy (GVA). Measured in meters.

geohash.description:
Geohash of the geo-coordinates (latitude and longitude).

Geohashing is a geocoding system used to encode geographic coordinates in decimal degrees, to a single string.

horizontal_accuracy.description: Provides quality/containment on horizontal position. This is based on ADS-B NACp. Measured in meters.

is_on_premises.description: Indicates whether the location is on-premises.

isp.description: The name of the Internet Service Provider (ISP).

lat.description: The geographical Latitude coordinate represented in Decimal Degrees (DD). For example: 42.361145.

long.description: The geographical Longitude coordinate represented in Decimal Degrees (DD). For example: -71.057083.

postal_code.description: The postal code of the location.

pressure_altitude.description: The uncorrected barometric pressure altitude (based on reference standard 29.92 inHg, 1013.25 mb) provides a reference for algorithms that utilize 'altitude deltas' between aircraft. This value is provided in meters and must have a minimum resolution of 1 m.. Special Values: Invalid, No Value, or Unknown: -1000 m.

provider.description: The provider of the geographical location data.

region.description: The alphanumeric code that identifies the principal subdivision (e.g. province or state) of the country. For example, 'CH-VD' for the Canton of Vaud, Switzerland

OcsfLocation.title: OcsfLocation

OcsfLogger.description: The Logger object represents the device and product where events are stored with times for receipt and transmission.  This may be at the source device where the event occurred, a remote scanning device, intermediate hops, or the ultimate destination.

device.description: The device where the events are logged.

event_uid.description: The unique identifier of the event assigned by the logger.

is_truncated.description: Indicates whether the OCSF event data has been truncated due to size limitations. When true, some event data may have been omitted to fit within system constraints.

log_format.description: The format of data in the log. For example JSON, syslog or CSV.

log_level.description: The level at which an event was logged. This can be log provider specific. For example the audit level.

log_name.description: The log name for the logging provider log, or the file name of the system log. This may be an intermediate store-and-forward log or a vendor destination log. For example /archive/server1/var/log/messages.0 or /var/log/.

log_provider.description: The logging provider or logging service that logged the event. This may be an intermediate application store-and-forward log or a vendor destination log.

log_version.description: The event log schema version of the original event. For example the syslog version or the Cisco Log Schema version

logged_time.description: The time when this logger received and logged the event. For the last logger in the pipeline, this value should match metadata.logged_time.

logged_time_dt.description: The time when this logger received and logged the event. For the last logger in the pipeline, this value should match metadata.logged_time.

name.description: The name of the logging product instance.

product.description: The product logging the event.  This may be the event source product, a management server product, a scanning product, a SIEM, etc.

transmit_time.description: The time when the event was transmitted from the logging device to it's next destination.

transmit_time_dt.description: The time when the event was transmitted from the logging device to it's next destination.

uid.description: The unique identifier of the logging product instance.

uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

untruncated_size.description: The original size of the OCSF event data in kilobytes before any truncation occurred. This field is typically populated when is_truncated is true to indicate the full size of the original event.

version.description: The version of the logging provider.

OcsfLogger.title: OcsfLogger

OcsfLongString.description: This object is a used to capture strings which may be truncated by a security product due to their length.

is_truncated.description: Indicates that value has been truncated. May be omitted if truncation has not occurred.

untruncated_size.description: The size in bytes of the string represented by value before truncation. Should be omitted if truncation has not occurred.

value.description: The string value, truncated if is_truncated is true.

OcsfLongString.title: OcsfLongString

OcsfMacosUsersProfile.description: The attributes that macOS uses to identify user information.

egid.description: The effective group under which this process is running.

euid.description: The effective user under which this process is running.

OcsfMacosUsersProfile.title: OcsfMacosUsersProfile

OcsfMalware.description: The Malware object describes the classification of known malicious software, which is intentionally designed to cause damage to a computer, server, client, or computer network.

classification_ids.description: The list of normalized identifiers of the malware classifications.

anyOf.description: The classification is unknown.
The classification is not mapped. See the classifications attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

classifications.description: The list of malware classifications, normalized to the captions of the classification_ids values. In the case of 'Other', they are defined by the event source.

cves.description: The list of Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVE) identifiers associated with the malware.

files.description: The list of file objects representing files that were identified as infected by the malware.

name.description: The malware name, as reported by the detection engine.

num_infected.description: The number of files that were identified to be infected by the malware.

path.description: The filesystem path of the malware that was observed.

provider.description: The name or identifier of the security solution or service that provided the malware detection information.

severity.description: The severity of the malware, normalized to the captions of the severity_id values. In the case of 'Other', they are defined by the event source.

anyOf.description: The event/finding severity is unknown.
Informational message. No action required.
The user decides if action is needed.
Action is required but the situation is not serious at this time.
Action is required immediately.
Action is required immediately and the scope is broad.
An error occurred but it is too late to take remedial action.
The event/finding severity is not mapped. See the severity attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

severity_id.description: The normalized identifier of the malware severity.

uid.description: A unique identifier for the specific malware instance, as assigned by the detection engine (e.g., virus signature ID or IPS rule ID).

uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

OcsfMalware.title: OcsfMalware

OcsfMalwareScanInfo.description: The malware scan information object describes characteristics, metadata of a malware scanning job.

end_time.description: The timestamp indicating when the scan job completed execution.

end_time_dt.description: The timestamp indicating when the scan job completed execution.

name.description: The administrator-supplied or application-generated name of the scan. For example: "Home office weekly user database scan", "Scan folders for viruses", "Full system virus scan"

num_files.description: The total number of files analyzed during the scan.

num_infected.description: The total number of files identified as infected with malware during the scan.

num_volumes.description: The total number of storage volumes examined during the malware scan.

size.description: The total size in bytes of all files that were scanned.

start_time.description: The timestamp indicating when the scan job began execution.

start_time_dt.description: The timestamp indicating when the scan job began execution.

type.description: The type of scan.

anyOf.description: The type is unknown.
The scan was manually initiated by the user or administrator.
The scan was started based on scheduler.
The scan was triggered by a content update.
The scan was triggered by newly quarantined items.
The scan was triggered by the attachment of removable media.
The scan was started due to a user logon.
The scan was triggered by an Early Launch Anti-Malware (ELAM) detection.
The scan type id is not mapped. See the type attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

type_id.description: The type id of the scan.

uid.description: The application-defined unique identifier assigned to an instance of a scan.

uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

unique_malware_count.description: The number of unique malware detected across all infected files.

OcsfMalwareScanInfo.title: OcsfMalwareScanInfo

OcsfManagedEntity.description: The Managed Entity object describes the type and version of an entity, such as a user, device, or policy. For types in the type_id enum list, an associated attribute should be populated. If the type of entity is not in the type_id list, information can be put into the data attribute, type_id should be 'Other' and the type attribute should label the entity type.

data.description: The managed entity content as a JSON object.

device.description: An addressable device, computer system or host.

group.description: The group object associated with an entity such as user, policy, or rule.

location.description: The detailed geographical location usually associated with an IP address.

name.description: The name of the managed entity. It should match the name of the specific entity object's name if populated, or the name of the managed entity if the type_id is 'Other'.

org.description: The Organization object containing details about the managed organizational entity. This object includes properties such as the organization name, unique identifier, type, and other organizational metadata. This attribute should be populated when type_id is 4 (Organization).

policy.description: Describes details of a managed policy.

type.description: The managed entity type. For example: Policy, User, Organization, Device.

anyOf.description: The type is unknown.
A managed Device entity. This item corresponds to population of the device attribute.
A managed User entity. This item corresponds to population of the user attribute.
A managed Group entity. This item corresponds to population of the group attribute.
A managed Organization entity. This item corresponds to population of the org attribute.
A managed Policy entity. This item corresponds to population of the policy attribute.
A managed Email entity. This item corresponds to population of the email attribute.
A managed Network Zone entity. Populate the name attribute with the zone name and/or the uid attribute with the zone ID. Additional zone information can be added to the data attribute.
The type is not mapped. See the type attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

type_id.description: The type of the Managed Entity. It is recommended to also populate the type attribute with the associated label, or the source specific name if Other.

uid.description: The identifier of the managed entity. It should match the uid of the specific entity's object UID if populated, or the source specific ID if the type_id is 'Other'.

uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

user.description: The user that pertains to the event or object.

version.description: The version of the managed entity. For example: 1.2.3.

OcsfManagedEntity.title: OcsfManagedEntity

OcsfMemoryActivity.description: Memory Activity events report when a process has memory allocated, read/modified, or other manipulation activities - such as a buffer overflow or turning off data execution protection (DEP).

anyOf.description: The action was unknown. The disposition_id attribute may still be set to a non-unknown value, for example 'Custom Action', 'Challenge'.
The activity was allowed. The disposition_id attribute should be set to a value that conforms to this action, for example 'Allowed', 'Approved', 'Delayed', 'No Action', 'Count' etc.

The attempted activity was denied. The disposition_id attribute should be set to a value that conforms to this action, for example 'Blocked', 'Rejected', 'Quarantined', 'Isolated', 'Dropped', 'Access Revoked, etc.

The activity was observed, but neither explicitly allowed nor denied. This is common with IDS and EDR controls that report additional information on observed behavior such as TTPs. The disposition_id attribute should be set to a value that conforms to this action, for example 'Logged', 'Alert', 'Detected', 'Count', etc.
The activity was modified, adjusted, or corrected. The disposition_id attribute should be set appropriately, for example 'Restored', 'Corrected', 'Delayed', 'Captcha', 'Tagged'.
The action is not mapped. See the action attribute which contains a data source specific value.

action_id.description: The action taken by a control or other policy-based system leading to an outcome or disposition. An unknown action may still correspond to a known disposition. Refer to disposition_id for the outcome of the action.

anyOf.description: The event activity is unknown.
Data Execution Permission
Data Execution Permission
Read (Example: ReadProcessMemory)
Write (Example: WriteProcessMemory)
Map View (Example: MapViewOfFile2)
The event activity is not mapped. See the activity_name attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

activity_id.description: The normalized identifier of the activity that triggered the event. Each event class defines its own set of activity values. Use 0 (Unknown) when the activity cannot be determined. Use 99 (Other) when the activity does not match any defined value, in which case activity_name must be populated with the source-specific label.

activity_name.description: The event activity name, as defined by the activity_id. When activity_id is 99 (Other), this attribute must contain the source-specific activity label. For all other activity_id values, this must match the caption defined for that activity_id enum value.

actor.description: The user, process, or service that initiated the activity on the host. For system-level events this is typically a process; for IAM events it is typically a user or role.

actual_permissions.description: The permissions that were granted to access memory.

ai_agent.description: The autonomous AI agent that performed this operation. Carries model identity via ai_agent.ai_model. Populate when the action was performed by an agent rather than a direct model call.

ai_model.description: The AI model involved in this operation. Use for direct model invocations where no autonomous agent is involved. For agent-mediated operations, model identity is carried within ai_agent.ai_model instead.

api.description: Describes details about a typical API (Application Programming Interface) call.

attacks.description: An array of MITRE ATT&CK® objects describing identified tactics, techniques & sub-techniques. The objects are compatible with MITRE ATLAS™ tactics, techniques & sub-techniques.

attestation_list.description: One or more cryptographic attestation objects over an event, each providing integrity, authenticity, and non-repudiation. Independent attesters over the same event — for example a producer at write time and a downstream processor at ingest — each contribute a separate attestation, distinct from co-signers on a single attestation, which share its signatures array. Carried on the record_integrity profile; the object itself is domain-agnostic.

authorizations.description: Provides details about an authorization, such as authorization outcome, and any associated policies related to the activity/event.

base_address.description: The memory address that was access or requested.

category_name.description: The event category name, as defined by category_uid value: System Activity.

category_uid.description: The category unique identifier of the event. Each event class belongs to exactly one category. Producers and mappers must set this to the category defined by the event class being used.

class_name.description: The event class name, as defined by class_uid value: Memory Activity.

class_uid.description: The unique identifier of a class. A class describes the attributes available in an event. Producers and mappers must set this to the uid defined in the event class definition. For example, Detection Finding is 2004.

cloud.description: Describes details about the Cloud environment where the event or finding was created.

confidence.description: The confidence, normalized to the caption of the confidence_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

anyOf.description: The normalized confidence is unknown.
The confidence is not mapped to the defined enum values. See the confidence attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

confidence_id.description: The normalized confidence refers to the accuracy of the security control or alert. An analytic with a low confidence means that the alerts may be noisy or may not be malicious in nature.

confidence_score.description: The confidence score as reported by the event source. If confidence_id is 99 'Other', it should be the same as confidence if both are populated.

count.description: The number of events aggregated into this single record. Only populate for aggregate events. When set, start_time and end_time should also be provided to define the aggregation window.

delegation.description: The delegation under whose authority this AI operation was performed. Links the event to a durable authorization context independent of traces and sessions, enabling correlation of all events executed under the same delegated authority.

device.description: The host or device where the activity was observed. Populate with details such as hostname, IP address, OS, and hardware identifiers when available from the source.

disposition.description: The disposition name, normalized to the caption of the disposition_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

anyOf.description: The disposition is unknown.
Granted access or allowed the action to the protected resource.
Denied access or blocked the action to the protected resource.
A suspicious file or other content was moved to a benign location.
A session was isolated on the network or within a browser.
A file or other content was deleted.
The request was detected as a threat and resulted in the connection being dropped.
A custom action was executed such as running of a command script. Use the message attribute of the base class for details.
A request or submission was approved. For example, when a form was properly filled out and submitted. This is distinct from 1 'Allowed'.
A quarantined file or other content was restored to its original location.
A suspicious or risky entity was deemed to no longer be suspicious (re-scored).
A corrupt file or configuration was corrected.
A corrupt file or configuration was partially corrected.
A corrupt file or configuration was not corrected.
An operation was delayed, for example if a restart was required to finish the operation.
Suspicious activity or a policy violation was detected without further action.
The outcome of an operation had no action taken.
The operation or action was logged without further action.
A file or other entity was marked with extended attributes.
The request or activity was detected as a threat and resulted in a notification but request was not blocked.
Counted the request or activity but did not determine whether to allow it or block it.
The request was detected as a threat and resulted in the connection being reset.
Required the end user to solve a CAPTCHA puzzle to prove that a human being is sending the request.
Ran a silent challenge that required the client session to verify that it's a browser, and not a bot.
The requestor's access has been revoked due to security policy enforcements. Note: use the Host profile if the User or Actor requestor is not present in the event class.
A request or submission was rejected. For example, when a form was improperly filled out and submitted. This is distinct from 2 'Blocked'.

An attempt to access a resource was denied due to an authorization check that failed. This is a more specific disposition than 2 'Blocked' and can be complemented with the authorizations attribute for more detail.
An error occurred during the processing of the activity or request. Use the message attribute of the base class for details.
The disposition is not mapped. See the disposition attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

disposition_id.description: Describes the outcome or action taken by a security control, such as access control checks, malware detections or various types of policy violations.

duration.description: The elapsed time of the aggregation window in milliseconds, from start_time to end_time. Only populate for aggregate events (count > 1). The value should equal end_time - start_time.

end_time.description: The time of the most recent event in an aggregate (count > 1). Do not populate for discrete, point-in-time events - use time alone. Subclasses such as findings may redefine this for their own time-range semantics.

end_time_dt.description: The time of the most recent event in an aggregate (count > 1). Do not populate for discrete, point-in-time events - use time alone. Subclasses such as findings may redefine this for their own time-range semantics.

enrichments.description:
The additional information from an external data source, which is associated with the event or a finding. For example add location information for the IP address in the DNS answers:

[{"name": "answers.ip", "value": "92.24.47.250", "type": "location", "data": {"city": "Socotra", "continent": "Asia", "coordinates": [-25.4153, 17.0743], "country": "YE", "desc": "Yemen"}}]

firewall_rule.description: The firewall rule that pertains to the control that triggered the event, if applicable.

is_alert.description: Indicates that the event is considered to be an alertable signal. Should be set to true if disposition_id = Alert among other dispositions, and/or risk_level_id or severity_id of the event is elevated. Not all control events will be alertable, for example if disposition_id = Exonerated or disposition_id = Allowed.

malware.description: A list of Malware objects, describing details about the identified malware.

malware_scan_info.description: Describes details about the scan job that identified malware on the target system.

message.description: A human-readable description of the event, as defined by the source. This should be a concise, meaningful summary suitable for display in a UI or alert notification - not a raw log line. For example: "User john_doe logged in from 10.0.0.1." rather than a raw syslog string.

message_context.description: Communication context for AI system interactions including protocols, roles, clients, and session information for MCP and other AI communication systems.

metadata.description: The metadata object describes the event producer, schema version, and processing information. Producers and mappers must populate metadata.product to identify the data source, and metadata.version to indicate the OCSF schema version used. Consumers rely on this to interpret the event correctly.

observables.description: The observables array surfaces key indicators and entities from the event or finding in a single, consistent location for downstream correlation and detection. Each entry references an attribute path within the event (e.g., src_endpoint.ip) along with its type and value, enabling consumers to extract IOCs without parsing the full event structure.

osint.description: The OSINT (Open Source Intelligence) object contains details related to an indicator such as the indicator itself, related indicators, geolocation, registrar information, subdomains, analyst commentary, and other contextual information. This information can be used to further enrich a detection or finding by providing decisioning support to other analysts and engineers.

policy.description: The policy that pertains to the control that triggered the event, if applicable. For example the name of an anti-malware policy or an access control policy.

process.description: The process that had memory allocated, read/written, or had other manipulation activities performed on it.

raw_data.description: The original event/finding data as received from the source, before normalization into OCSF. Populate this with the verbatim log line, JSON payload, or other native format for forensic and debugging purposes. This field is not intended for structured querying - use the normalized OCSF attributes instead.

raw_data_hash.description: A fingerprint (hash) of the raw_data content. Use this to verify the integrity of the original event data or to deduplicate events.

raw_data_size.description: The size of the original event data (as captured in raw_data) in bytes, before OCSF normalization. Useful for metering and capacity planning.

requested_permissions.description: The permissions mask that was requested to access memory.

risk_details.description: Describes the risk associated with the finding.

risk_level.description: The risk level, normalized to the caption of the risk_level_id value.

anyOf.description: The risk level is not mapped. See the risk_level attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

risk_score.description: The risk score as reported by the event source.

severity.description: The event/finding severity label, normalized to the caption of the severity_id value. When severity_id is 99 (Other), this attribute must contain the source-specific severity label. For all other values, this should match the caption defined for that severity_id enum value (e.g., "High" for severity_id: 4).

anyOf.description: The event/finding severity is unknown.
Informational message. No action required.
The user decides if action is needed.
Action is required but the situation is not serious at this time.
Action is required immediately.
Action is required immediately and the scope is broad.
An error occurred but it is too late to take remedial action.
The event/finding severity is not mapped. See the severity attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

severity_id.description:
The normalized identifier of the event/finding severity.

The normalized severity is a measurement the effort and expense required to manage and resolve an event or incident. Smaller numerical values represent lower impact events, and larger numerical values represent higher impact events.

size.description: The memory size that was access or requested.

start_time.description: The time of the earliest event in an aggregate (count > 1). Do not populate for discrete, point-in-time events - use time alone. Subclasses such as findings may redefine this for their own time-range semantics.

start_time_dt.description: The time of the earliest event in an aggregate (count > 1). Do not populate for discrete, point-in-time events - use time alone. Subclasses such as findings may redefine this for their own time-range semantics.

status.description: The event status label, normalized to the caption of the status_id value. When status_id is 99 (Other), this attribute must contain the source-specific status label. For all other values, this must match the caption defined for that status_id enum value (e.g., "Success" for status_id: 1).

status_code.description: The source-specific status or error code as reported by the event source. For example, a Windows logon failure code (0x18), an HTTP response code (403), or an AWS API error code. This preserves the original code for detailed troubleshooting beyond what status_id conveys.

status_detail.description: A human-readable description providing additional context about the event outcome. Use this to convey details that go beyond the normalized status_id and source-specific status_code, such as a failure reason or error message. For example: "Account locked after 5 failed attempts.".

anyOf.description: The status is unknown.
The activity completed successfully.
The activity failed.
The status is not mapped. See the status attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

status_id.description: The normalized status of the event outcome. Use this family of attributes to convey the outcome of the activity described by the event. Producers should map their source outcome to 1 (Success) or 2 (Failure). Use 0 (Unknown) when the outcome cannot be determined, and 99 (Other) with a populated status string when the source value does not map cleanly.

time.description: The primary timestamp of the event - when the activity actually occurred at the source. This does not capture when the event record was created or serialized by the source system; for event lifecycle timestamps such as ingestion and processing, use metadata.logged_time and metadata.processed_time respectively, or the equivalent attributes in the metadata.loggers array when recording pipeline stages. For aggregate events (count > 1), set this to start_time (the earliest OCSF time in the aggregate) to preserve causal ordering and consistent timeline alignment. Note: finding classes redefine time as the finding creation time rather than the activity occurrence time. This must be a UTC epoch value in milliseconds (e.g., 1776881335332). Mappers should use the most precise and authoritative timestamp available from the source.

time_dt.description: The primary timestamp of the event - when the activity actually occurred at the source. This does not capture when the event record was created or serialized by the source system; for event lifecycle timestamps such as ingestion and processing, use metadata.logged_time and metadata.processed_time respectively, or the equivalent attributes in the metadata.loggers array when recording pipeline stages. For aggregate events (count > 1), set this to start_time (the earliest OCSF time in the aggregate) to preserve causal ordering and consistent timeline alignment. Note: finding classes redefine time as the finding creation time rather than the activity occurrence time. This must be a UTC epoch value in milliseconds (e.g., 1776881335332). Mappers should use the most precise and authoritative timestamp available from the source.

timezone_offset.description: The number of minutes that the reported event time is ahead or behind UTC, in the range -1,080 to +1,080. This allows consumers to reconstruct the local time at the event source. For example, US Eastern Standard Time is -300. Populate this when the source provides local time zone information.

type_name.description: The event/finding type name, combining the class and activity (e.g., "Detection Finding: Create"). The value must match the class_name and activity_name joined by ": ".

anyOf.description: Data Execution Permission
Data Execution Permission
Read (Example: ReadProcessMemory)
Write (Example: WriteProcessMemory)
Map View (Example: MapViewOfFile2)

type_uid.description: The event/finding type ID. It identifies the event's semantics and structure. Producers and mappers must compute this as class_uid * 100 + activity_id. It uniquely identifies the combination of event class and activity across the entire schema. For example, Detection Finding: Create is 200401.

unmapped.description:
A container for source-specific attributes that do not map to any defined OCSF attribute. Use this to preserve valuable source data that would otherwise be lost during normalization. The keys and values are specific to the event source.

Note: Consumers should not rely on a stable structure within this field. The preferred approach to unmapped attributes is to create a custom extension with the desired structure.

OcsfMemoryActivity.title: OcsfMemoryActivity

OcsfMessageContext.description: Communication context for AI system interactions including protocols, roles, clients, and session information for MCP and other AI communication systems.

anyOf.description: Unknown role type.
The human user initiating a request.
The AI model generating a response.
A callable tool or API invoked by the assistant.
A software agent that performs tasks with autonomy or delegated intent.
The component coordinating multiple agents or tools.
A component that retrieves information or context from a knowledge source (e.g., vector DB, search system, or API).
Other role type not covered above.

ai_role_id.description: Specifies the functional role of the AI within the context of this message, such as retrieving information, assisting reasoning, executing a tool, or generating content.

application.description: The initiating client application. In AI systems, this represents the client-side application or framework that initiates requests (e.g., LangChain application, web browser, mobile app, SDK implementation).

completion_tokens.description: Number of tokens in the model's response/completion for this message.

name.description: The name or identifier of the message context. In AI systems, this could be the conversation ID, session name, thread identifier, or interaction name (e.g., 'user-session-123', 'conversation-abc', 'chat-thread-456').

prompt_text.description: The text of the input prompt provided to the model for this message. This is the verbatim instruction, query, or context supplied to the AI system that drove the operation.

prompt_tokens.description: Number of tokens in the input prompt for this message.

response_text.description: The text of the model's response generated for this message. For agent-mediated operations, this is the content returned by the assistant, tool, or agent.

service.description: The server or service handling the request. In AI systems, this represents the AI service, API endpoint, or agent that processes and responds to requests (e.g., OpenAI API service, Claude API service, internal AI model service).

total_tokens.description: Total number of tokens used for this message (prompt + completion).

uid.description: The unique identifier of the message context. This could be a session ID, conversation ID, or other unique identifier that allows correlation of messages within the same context.

uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

OcsfMessageContext.title: OcsfMessageContext

OcsfMetadata.description: The Metadata object describes the metadata associated with the event.

correlation_uid.description: A unique identifier used to correlate this OCSF event with other related OCSF events, distinct from the event's uid value. This enables linking multiple OCSF events that are part of the same activity, transaction, or security incident across different systems or time periods.

data_classification.description: The Data Classification object includes information about data classification levels and data category types.

data_classifications.description: A list of Data Classification objects, that include information about data classification levels and data category types, identified by a classifier.

debug.description: Debug information about non-fatal issues with this OCSF event. Each issue is a line in this string array.

event_code.description: The identifier of the original event. For example the numerical Windows Event Code or Cisco syslog code.

extension.description: The schema extension used to create the event.

extensions.description: The schema extensions used to create the event.

is_truncated.description: Indicates whether the OCSF event data has been truncated due to size limitations. When true, some event data may have been omitted to fit within system constraints.

labels.description: The list of labels attached to the event. For example: ["sample", "dev"]

log_format.description: The format of data in the log where the data originated. For example CSV, XML, Windows Multiline, JSON, syslog or Cisco Log Schema.

log_level.description: The level at which an event was logged. This can be log provider specific. For example the audit level.

log_name.description: The event log name, typically for the consumer of the event. For example, the storage bucket name, SIEM repository index name, etc.

log_provider.description: The logging provider or logging service that logged the event. For example AWS CloudWatch or Splunk.

log_source.description: The log system or component where the data originated. For example, a file path, syslog server name or a Windows hostname and logging subsystem such as Security.

log_version.description: The event log schema version of the original event. For example the syslog version or the Cisco Log Schema version

logged_time.description: The ultimate logged time in the event pipeline - when the event reached its final destination (e.g., SIEM, data lake). If loggers is populated, this should match the logged_time of the last entry in the loggers array. This is distinct from time (when the activity occurred) and processed_time (when an intermediate system processed the event).

logged_time_dt.description: The ultimate logged time in the event pipeline - when the event reached its final destination (e.g., SIEM, data lake). If loggers is populated, this should match the logged_time of the last entry in the loggers array. This is distinct from time (when the activity occurred) and processed_time (when an intermediate system processed the event).

loggers.description: An ordered array of Logger objects describing each hop in the event pipeline between the source and its final destination. Each entry captures the logging product, device, and timestamps (logged_time, transmit_time) at that stage. The last entry's logged_time should match metadata.logged_time.

modified_time.description: The time when the event was last modified or enriched.

modified_time_dt.description: The time when the event was last modified or enriched.

original_event_uid.description: The unique identifier assigned to the event in its original logging system before transformation to OCSF format. This field preserves the source system's native event identifier, enabling traceability back to the raw log entry. For example, a Windows Event Record ID, a syslog message ID, a Splunk _cd value, or a database transaction log sequence number.

original_time.description: The original event time as reported by the event source, preserved as a pass-through string in its native format (e.g., Syslog timestamp, Windows event time). This is not normalized to timestamp_t - the normalized equivalent is the base event time attribute. Omit if the event is generated rather than collected via logs.

processed_time.description: The time when the event was processed by an intermediate system (e.g., ETL pipeline, event processor) before reaching its final destination. Can be used with logged_time to calculate queuing duration via total_queued_duration.

processed_time_dt.description: The time when the event was processed by an intermediate system (e.g., ETL pipeline, event processor) before reaching its final destination. Can be used with logged_time to calculate queuing duration via total_queued_duration.

product.description: The product that reported the event.

profiles.description: The list of profiles used to create the event. Profiles should be referenced by their name attribute for core profiles, or extension/name for profiles from extensions.

reporter.description: The entity from which the event or finding was first reported.

sequence.description: Sequence number of the event. The sequence number is a value available in some events, to make the exact ordering of events unambiguous, regardless of the event time precision.

source.description: The source of the event or finding. This can be any distinguishing name for the logical origin of the data — for example, 'CloudTrail Events', or a use case like 'Attack Simulations' or 'Vulnerability Scans'.

tags.description: The list of tags; {key:value} pairs associated to the event.

total_queued_duration.description: The amount of time an event spent in a queue awaiting processing. In this case, the value is the difference between processed_time and logged_time. This duration is inclusive of all queues between the originator of the event and the intended long-term storage destination of the event.

transformation_info_list.description: An array of transformation info that describes the mappings or transforms applied to the data.

transmit_time.description: The time when the event was transmitted from the logging device to it's next destination.

transmit_time_dt.description: The time when the event was transmitted from the logging device to it's next destination.

type.description: The type of the event or finding as a subset of the source of the event. This can be any distinguishing characteristic of the data. For example 'Management Events' or 'Device Penetration Test'.

uid.description: A unique identifier assigned to the OCSF event. This ID is specific to the OCSF event itself and is distinct from the original event identifier in the source system (see original_event_uid).

untruncated_size.description: The original size of the OCSF event data in kilobytes before any truncation occurred. This field is typically populated when is_truncated is true to indicate the full size of the original event.

version.description: The version of the OCSF schema, using Semantic Versioning Specification (SemVer). For example: 1.0.0. Event consumers use the version to determine the available event attributes.

OcsfMetadata.title: OcsfMetadata

OcsfMetric.description: The Metric object defines a simple name/value pair entity for a metric.

name.description: The name of the metric.

OcsfMetric.title: OcsfMetric

OcsfMitigation.description: The MITRE Mitigation object describes the ATT&CK® or ATLAS™ Mitigation ID and/or name that is associated to an attack.

countermeasures.description: The D3FEND countermeasures that are associated with the attack technique. For example: ATT&CK Technique T1003 is addressed by Mitigation M1027, and D3FEND Technique D3-OTP.

name.description: The Mitigation name that is associated with the attack technique. For example: Password Policies, or Code Signing.

src_url.description: The versioned permalink of the Mitigation. For example: https://attack.mitre.org/versions/v14/mitigations/M1027.

uid.description: The Mitigation ID that is associated with the attack technique. For example: M1027, or AML.M0013.

uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

OcsfMitigation.title: OcsfMitigation

OcsfModule.description: The Module object describes the attributes of a module.

base_address.description: The memory address where the module was loaded.

file.description: The module file object.

function_invocation.description: Details about the invocation of the function given in function_name.

function_name.description: The invoked function in the module. For load and unload events, this is the entry-point function of the module. The system calls the entry-point function whenever a process or thread loads or unloads the module.

load_type.description: The load type, normalized to the caption of the load_type_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

anyOf.description: The load type is unknown.
A normal module loaded by the normal windows loading mechanism i.e. LoadLibrary.
A module loaded in a way avoidant of normal windows procedures. i.e. Bootstrapped Loading/Manual Dll Loading.
A raw module in process memory that is READWRITE_EXECUTE and had a thread started in its range.
A memory mapped file, typically created with CreatefileMapping/MapViewOfFile.
A module loaded in a non standard way. However, GetModuleFileName succeeds on this allocation.
The load type is not mapped. See the load_type attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

load_type_id.description: The normalized identifier for how the module was loaded in memory.

start_address.description: The start address of the execution.

type.description: The module type.

OcsfModule.title: OcsfModule

OcsfModuleActivity.description: Module Activity events report when an endpoint process acts on a module.

anyOf.description: The action was unknown. The disposition_id attribute may still be set to a non-unknown value, for example 'Custom Action', 'Challenge'.
The activity was allowed. The disposition_id attribute should be set to a value that conforms to this action, for example 'Allowed', 'Approved', 'Delayed', 'No Action', 'Count' etc.

The attempted activity was denied. The disposition_id attribute should be set to a value that conforms to this action, for example 'Blocked', 'Rejected', 'Quarantined', 'Isolated', 'Dropped', 'Access Revoked, etc.

The activity was observed, but neither explicitly allowed nor denied. This is common with IDS and EDR controls that report additional information on observed behavior such as TTPs. The disposition_id attribute should be set to a value that conforms to this action, for example 'Logged', 'Alert', 'Detected', 'Count', etc.
The activity was modified, adjusted, or corrected. The disposition_id attribute should be set appropriately, for example 'Restored', 'Corrected', 'Delayed', 'Captcha', 'Tagged'.
The action is not mapped. See the action attribute which contains a data source specific value.

action_id.description: The action taken by a control or other policy-based system leading to an outcome or disposition. An unknown action may still correspond to a known disposition. Refer to disposition_id for the outcome of the action.

anyOf.description: The event activity is unknown.
The target module was loaded.
The target module was unloaded.
A function exported from the target module was invoked.
The event activity is not mapped. See the activity_name attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

activity_id.description: The normalized identifier of the activity that triggered the event. Each event class defines its own set of activity values. Use 0 (Unknown) when the activity cannot be determined. Use 99 (Other) when the activity does not match any defined value, in which case activity_name must be populated with the source-specific label.

activity_name.description: The event activity name, as defined by the activity_id. When activity_id is 99 (Other), this attribute must contain the source-specific activity label. For all other activity_id values, this must match the caption defined for that activity_id enum value.

actor.description: The actor that performed the activity on the target module. For example, the process that loaded a module into memory.

ai_agent.description: The autonomous AI agent that performed this operation. Carries model identity via ai_agent.ai_model. Populate when the action was performed by an agent rather than a direct model call.

ai_model.description: The AI model involved in this operation. Use for direct model invocations where no autonomous agent is involved. For agent-mediated operations, model identity is carried within ai_agent.ai_model instead.

api.description: Describes details about a typical API (Application Programming Interface) call.

attacks.description: An array of MITRE ATT&CK® objects describing identified tactics, techniques & sub-techniques. The objects are compatible with MITRE ATLAS™ tactics, techniques & sub-techniques.

attestation_list.description: One or more cryptographic attestation objects over an event, each providing integrity, authenticity, and non-repudiation. Independent attesters over the same event — for example a producer at write time and a downstream processor at ingest — each contribute a separate attestation, distinct from co-signers on a single attestation, which share its signatures array. Carried on the record_integrity profile; the object itself is domain-agnostic.

authorizations.description: Provides details about an authorization, such as authorization outcome, and any associated policies related to the activity/event.

category_name.description: The event category name, as defined by category_uid value: System Activity.

category_uid.description: The category unique identifier of the event. Each event class belongs to exactly one category. Producers and mappers must set this to the category defined by the event class being used.

class_name.description: The event class name, as defined by class_uid value: Module Activity.

class_uid.description: The unique identifier of a class. A class describes the attributes available in an event. Producers and mappers must set this to the uid defined in the event class definition. For example, Detection Finding is 2004.

cloud.description: Describes details about the Cloud environment where the event or finding was created.

confidence.description: The confidence, normalized to the caption of the confidence_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

anyOf.description: The normalized confidence is unknown.
The confidence is not mapped to the defined enum values. See the confidence attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

confidence_id.description: The normalized confidence refers to the accuracy of the security control or alert. An analytic with a low confidence means that the alerts may be noisy or may not be malicious in nature.

confidence_score.description: The confidence score as reported by the event source. If confidence_id is 99 'Other', it should be the same as confidence if both are populated.

count.description: The number of events aggregated into this single record. Only populate for aggregate events. When set, start_time and end_time should also be provided to define the aggregation window.

delegation.description: The delegation under whose authority this AI operation was performed. Links the event to a durable authorization context independent of traces and sessions, enabling correlation of all events executed under the same delegated authority.

device.description: The host or device where the activity was observed. Populate with details such as hostname, IP address, OS, and hardware identifiers when available from the source.

disposition.description: The disposition name, normalized to the caption of the disposition_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

anyOf.description: The disposition is unknown.
Granted access or allowed the action to the protected resource.
Denied access or blocked the action to the protected resource.
A suspicious file or other content was moved to a benign location.
A session was isolated on the network or within a browser.
A file or other content was deleted.
The request was detected as a threat and resulted in the connection being dropped.
A custom action was executed such as running of a command script. Use the message attribute of the base class for details.
A request or submission was approved. For example, when a form was properly filled out and submitted. This is distinct from 1 'Allowed'.
A quarantined file or other content was restored to its original location.
A suspicious or risky entity was deemed to no longer be suspicious (re-scored).
A corrupt file or configuration was corrected.
A corrupt file or configuration was partially corrected.
A corrupt file or configuration was not corrected.
An operation was delayed, for example if a restart was required to finish the operation.
Suspicious activity or a policy violation was detected without further action.
The outcome of an operation had no action taken.
The operation or action was logged without further action.
A file or other entity was marked with extended attributes.
The request or activity was detected as a threat and resulted in a notification but request was not blocked.
Counted the request or activity but did not determine whether to allow it or block it.
The request was detected as a threat and resulted in the connection being reset.
Required the end user to solve a CAPTCHA puzzle to prove that a human being is sending the request.
Ran a silent challenge that required the client session to verify that it's a browser, and not a bot.
The requestor's access has been revoked due to security policy enforcements. Note: use the Host profile if the User or Actor requestor is not present in the event class.
A request or submission was rejected. For example, when a form was improperly filled out and submitted. This is distinct from 2 'Blocked'.

An attempt to access a resource was denied due to an authorization check that failed. This is a more specific disposition than 2 'Blocked' and can be complemented with the authorizations attribute for more detail.
An error occurred during the processing of the activity or request. Use the message attribute of the base class for details.
The disposition is not mapped. See the disposition attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

disposition_id.description: Describes the outcome or action taken by a security control, such as access control checks, malware detections or various types of policy violations.

duration.description: The elapsed time of the aggregation window in milliseconds, from start_time to end_time. Only populate for aggregate events (count > 1). The value should equal end_time - start_time.

end_time.description: The time of the most recent event in an aggregate (count > 1). Do not populate for discrete, point-in-time events - use time alone. Subclasses such as findings may redefine this for their own time-range semantics.

end_time_dt.description: The time of the most recent event in an aggregate (count > 1). Do not populate for discrete, point-in-time events - use time alone. Subclasses such as findings may redefine this for their own time-range semantics.

enrichments.description:
The additional information from an external data source, which is associated with the event or a finding. For example add location information for the IP address in the DNS answers:

[{"name": "answers.ip", "value": "92.24.47.250", "type": "location", "data": {"city": "Socotra", "continent": "Asia", "coordinates": [-25.4153, 17.0743], "country": "YE", "desc": "Yemen"}}]

firewall_rule.description: The firewall rule that pertains to the control that triggered the event, if applicable.

is_alert.description: Indicates that the event is considered to be an alertable signal. Should be set to true if disposition_id = Alert among other dispositions, and/or risk_level_id or severity_id of the event is elevated. Not all control events will be alertable, for example if disposition_id = Exonerated or disposition_id = Allowed.

malware.description: A list of Malware objects, describing details about the identified malware.

malware_scan_info.description: Describes details about the scan job that identified malware on the target system.

message.description: A human-readable description of the event, as defined by the source. This should be a concise, meaningful summary suitable for display in a UI or alert notification - not a raw log line. For example: "User john_doe logged in from 10.0.0.1." rather than a raw syslog string.

message_context.description: Communication context for AI system interactions including protocols, roles, clients, and session information for MCP and other AI communication systems.

metadata.description: The metadata object describes the event producer, schema version, and processing information. Producers and mappers must populate metadata.product to identify the data source, and metadata.version to indicate the OCSF schema version used. Consumers rely on this to interpret the event correctly.

module.description: The module that was loaded, unloaded, or invoked.

observables.description: The observables array surfaces key indicators and entities from the event or finding in a single, consistent location for downstream correlation and detection. Each entry references an attribute path within the event (e.g., src_endpoint.ip) along with its type and value, enabling consumers to extract IOCs without parsing the full event structure.

osint.description: The OSINT (Open Source Intelligence) object contains details related to an indicator such as the indicator itself, related indicators, geolocation, registrar information, subdomains, analyst commentary, and other contextual information. This information can be used to further enrich a detection or finding by providing decisioning support to other analysts and engineers.

policy.description: The policy that pertains to the control that triggered the event, if applicable. For example the name of an anti-malware policy or an access control policy.

raw_data.description: The original event/finding data as received from the source, before normalization into OCSF. Populate this with the verbatim log line, JSON payload, or other native format for forensic and debugging purposes. This field is not intended for structured querying - use the normalized OCSF attributes instead.

raw_data_hash.description: A fingerprint (hash) of the raw_data content. Use this to verify the integrity of the original event data or to deduplicate events.

raw_data_size.description: The size of the original event data (as captured in raw_data) in bytes, before OCSF normalization. Useful for metering and capacity planning.

risk_details.description: Describes the risk associated with the finding.

risk_level.description: The risk level, normalized to the caption of the risk_level_id value.

anyOf.description: The risk level is not mapped. See the risk_level attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

risk_score.description: The risk score as reported by the event source.

severity.description: The event/finding severity label, normalized to the caption of the severity_id value. When severity_id is 99 (Other), this attribute must contain the source-specific severity label. For all other values, this should match the caption defined for that severity_id enum value (e.g., "High" for severity_id: 4).

anyOf.description: The event/finding severity is unknown.
Informational message. No action required.
The user decides if action is needed.
Action is required but the situation is not serious at this time.
Action is required immediately.
Action is required immediately and the scope is broad.
An error occurred but it is too late to take remedial action.
The event/finding severity is not mapped. See the severity attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

severity_id.description:
The normalized identifier of the event/finding severity.

The normalized severity is a measurement the effort and expense required to manage and resolve an event or incident. Smaller numerical values represent lower impact events, and larger numerical values represent higher impact events.

start_time.description: The time of the earliest event in an aggregate (count > 1). Do not populate for discrete, point-in-time events - use time alone. Subclasses such as findings may redefine this for their own time-range semantics.

start_time_dt.description: The time of the earliest event in an aggregate (count > 1). Do not populate for discrete, point-in-time events - use time alone. Subclasses such as findings may redefine this for their own time-range semantics.

status.description: The event status label, normalized to the caption of the status_id value. When status_id is 99 (Other), this attribute must contain the source-specific status label. For all other values, this must match the caption defined for that status_id enum value (e.g., "Success" for status_id: 1).

status_code.description: The source-specific status or error code as reported by the event source. For example, a Windows logon failure code (0x18), an HTTP response code (403), or an AWS API error code. This preserves the original code for detailed troubleshooting beyond what status_id conveys.

status_detail.description: A human-readable description providing additional context about the event outcome. Use this to convey details that go beyond the normalized status_id and source-specific status_code, such as a failure reason or error message. For example: "Account locked after 5 failed attempts.".

anyOf.description: The status is unknown.
The activity completed successfully.
The activity failed.
The status is not mapped. See the status attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

status_id.description: The normalized status of the event outcome. Use this family of attributes to convey the outcome of the activity described by the event. Producers should map their source outcome to 1 (Success) or 2 (Failure). Use 0 (Unknown) when the outcome cannot be determined, and 99 (Other) with a populated status string when the source value does not map cleanly.

time.description: The primary timestamp of the event - when the activity actually occurred at the source. This does not capture when the event record was created or serialized by the source system; for event lifecycle timestamps such as ingestion and processing, use metadata.logged_time and metadata.processed_time respectively, or the equivalent attributes in the metadata.loggers array when recording pipeline stages. For aggregate events (count > 1), set this to start_time (the earliest OCSF time in the aggregate) to preserve causal ordering and consistent timeline alignment. Note: finding classes redefine time as the finding creation time rather than the activity occurrence time. This must be a UTC epoch value in milliseconds (e.g., 1776881335332). Mappers should use the most precise and authoritative timestamp available from the source.

time_dt.description: The primary timestamp of the event - when the activity actually occurred at the source. This does not capture when the event record was created or serialized by the source system; for event lifecycle timestamps such as ingestion and processing, use metadata.logged_time and metadata.processed_time respectively, or the equivalent attributes in the metadata.loggers array when recording pipeline stages. For aggregate events (count > 1), set this to start_time (the earliest OCSF time in the aggregate) to preserve causal ordering and consistent timeline alignment. Note: finding classes redefine time as the finding creation time rather than the activity occurrence time. This must be a UTC epoch value in milliseconds (e.g., 1776881335332). Mappers should use the most precise and authoritative timestamp available from the source.

timezone_offset.description: The number of minutes that the reported event time is ahead or behind UTC, in the range -1,080 to +1,080. This allows consumers to reconstruct the local time at the event source. For example, US Eastern Standard Time is -300. Populate this when the source provides local time zone information.

type_name.description: The event/finding type name, combining the class and activity (e.g., "Detection Finding: Create"). The value must match the class_name and activity_name joined by ": ".

anyOf.description: The target module was loaded.
The target module was unloaded.
A function exported from the target module was invoked.

type_uid.description: The event/finding type ID. It identifies the event's semantics and structure. Producers and mappers must compute this as class_uid * 100 + activity_id. It uniquely identifies the combination of event class and activity across the entire schema. For example, Detection Finding: Create is 200401.

unmapped.description:
A container for source-specific attributes that do not map to any defined OCSF attribute. Use this to preserve valuable source data that would otherwise be lost during normalization. The keys and values are specific to the event source.

Note: Consumers should not rely on a stable structure within this field. The preferred approach to unmapped attributes is to create a custom extension with the desired structure.

anyOf.description: The event activity is unknown.
The discovered results are via a query request.
The event activity is not mapped. See the activity_name attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

activity_id.description: The normalized identifier of the activity that triggered the event. Each event class defines its own set of activity values. Use 0 (Unknown) when the activity cannot be determined. Use 99 (Other) when the activity does not match any defined value, in which case activity_name must be populated with the source-specific label.

activity_name.description: The event activity name, as defined by the activity_id. When activity_id is 99 (Other), this attribute must contain the source-specific activity label. For all other activity_id values, this must match the caption defined for that activity_id enum value.

actor.description: The user, process, or service that initiated the activity on the host. For system-level events this is typically a process; for IAM events it is typically a user or role.

api.description: Describes details about a typical API (Application Programming Interface) call.

attacks.description: An array of MITRE ATT&CK® objects describing identified tactics, techniques & sub-techniques. The objects are compatible with MITRE ATLAS™ tactics, techniques & sub-techniques.
